decisions.summary: git add is let through while the gate runs, on the premise that it moves nothing the gate checks
decisions.why: The premise is false, measured 2026-10-17 by this reviewer: preflight.py tree() keys on `git diff --name-only HEAD`, and in a scratch repo `git add` of an untracked file made it appear in that list (before: empty; after: 'new'), so tree_moved() reports it and the gate goes NOT GREEN. Staging a new file is the ordinary step before a commit, so the carve-out passes exactly the gate-voiding write FR-010 exists to stop (purpose-fatal). The earlier CLEAR text refused git add. Fix: refuse a git add that stages any path not already in `git diff --name-only HEAD` (a new file), or refuse git add whole; a git add of an already-modified tracked file may pass.

decisions.summary: make record-checked and make modal-triaged are let through as writing only under .git/
decisions.why: Adjudicated per target. modal-triaged: within - modal_triage.py record writes the store and its TOUCHED mark only, under .git/. record-checked: the premise is false for one of its forms - with REPLY= it runs record_owed.file_outside(), which appends to the active feature's specs/<NNN>/found.jsonl, a TRACKED file (git ls-files lists specs/335-.../found.jsonl and others), so it moves the tracked tree and voids the gate. (REASON= writes a new untracked file under dev/bypass-log/, which tree() does not see.) Fix: refuse make record-checked when REPLY= is given (or move found.jsonl writes to wait), and state the premise per form rather than for the target.

decisions.summary: Seed 21, exit (1): where a fouled way is a household's only route and it crosses a neighbor's yard, the household is reached across its neighbor (0246's fallback, R), but 'the way is not drawn through the yard, and the house counts as reached, as unreached_houses already allows.'
decisions.why: In amendment 1 the GM asked: 'Are we sure that household paths don't cut through neighbors' yards? I thought that our research findings were that they did.' The R label the plan carries attaches only to 'reached across a neighbor's yard'. The clause 'the way is not drawn through the yard' has no research basis in the plan. Its only stated ground is existing code (unreached_houses), and preserving existing behavior the GM did not ask to preserve does not make an exception legitimate. Here that behavior is the one the GM's question challenged: no path through a neighbor's yard. The blind block does not carry the clause ('0246's own fallback is reaching the house across a neighbor's yard'). The Decisions preface says that where block and session differ on seeds 17 and 21 'the decision names the measurement that settles it, not a side'. D20(1) takes a side and names no measurement, and FR-012 requires the plan to say where it differs from the blind block. It should say one of two things instead. (a) The household's way is drawn across the neighbor's yard, as an exception to fouled_segment for that case. Or (b) the decision quotes the 0246 line showing that such a crossing leaves no drawn path, labels 'not drawn' R on that line, and marks it as the session's difference from the blind block.

decisions.why: Room first is the GM's ruling and 'give it more room' is a checklist exit. The reader question is the GM's 'say that there isn't a problem' from amendment 1. The T04 route is ruled under D22-exit.

decisions.why: The GM's request names merging near-parallel close paths as 'adding a rule ... where the new rule did in fact solve the problem'; the approved proposal: 'Add a rule that removes the case, like merging two near-parallel paths'. A step that only adds merges is that rule. Moving REACH out of the refusal (part B 3, 5) stops tuning one number, which is the thrashing the request exists to end.

decisions.summary: A merge cut is written only where the cut way keeps the law (Lawful); otherwise the pair is left unmerged.
decisions.why: An 'only where' on the requested merge, so ruled as an exception, each residue case separately. (a) An unmendable pair within 14 ft is refused by the doubled-tail rule, exactly as before T03. (b) An unmendable pair at 14-20 ft is drawn as two ways, exactly as before T03. Neither case is worse than HEAD; the condition only declines to add a merge that would break the lane law. It is implied by the GM's own words: 'I don't want future sessions to just throw away rules when they are inconvenient', and the approved guardrail that loosening a rule needs its reason recorded - an unlawful cut would drop the law with no record. The bundle cannot show what Lawful contains: a merge T meets its partner within _DOUBLED_DEG of parallel, and if Lawful's meeting-angle rule vetoes such a T the step would be hollow and the exception purpose-fatal. The ruling therefore rests on D22's backstops, which fail if that happens: the merge test red first on Inashiro lanes 8 and 14 and seed 49's root way, and the Inashiro glyph-check re-run with F1-F3 gone. If either is met by narrowing them rather than by merges, this ruling does not hold.

decisions.why: Classified on this review's reading, not the plan's label. The refusal reaches only pairs the merge could not mend, so it narrows nothing the merge does; the number is O (part B 2), a knob left where T01 put it. The GM did not ask that refusal removed, and widening it to 20 ft is what refused household ways and a farmhouse (part B 1).

The plan does block, once, for the filing only, and never asks for a fix before the landing goes ahead, which is what option 3 was chosen for ('just not before this task lands'). Two concrete legs. (1) A push-time gate cannot put its filing into the commit being pushed, so 'the gate writes tasks.md and the landing goes ahead' leaves the open item only in a working tree while the code is on main. That defeats option 3's own guarantee that the feature cannot close with the finding open. decisions.summary: Past the hour, a dispatch within SAME_MESSAGE_S (5 s) of an admitted dispatch is admitted - the rest of the message the admitted one began
decisions.why: It narrows the hour guard (the GM's hourly step-back, 383): some dispatches past the hour are no longer refused. Presumed wrong. It survives on purpose and on the GM's own words. The step-back's purpose is that no new decision is taken after the hour without stepping back. The dispatches of one assistant message were all decided together, before the guard spoke, so the step-back cannot reach that decision. Refusing part of the message only splits it by hook latency (T05's five went two and three), and the refused part is re-dispatched after the step-back anyway (T05 part B item 9). The GM's amendment 5 ('I wonder if another tooling fix would make us more likely to batch commands') asks for more batching, and a guard that splits a batch penalizes exactly that. PREMISE this ruling rests on: the plan carries out 'same message' as nearness in time (5 s from an admitted dispatch), not as the message's identity. The ruling covers only the plan's stated bound, 'the rest of the message it began'. A window that admits a dispatch from a FOLLOWING message, for example one emitted within 5 s of a dispatch that returned at once, or a chain that carries past the message, would be outside this ruling and would need a new one. The test should hold that bound. Approach item 3's 'the batching hook's same-turn window, widened' is read as a wider value used by checkpoint.due only. D42 names only checkpoint.due and stepback_bundle.refusals. A change to the batching hook's own window would reach beyond the arbiter's fix.

decisions.why: A test whose only effect is to enforce the requested fix; enforcement of what was asked.

decisions.summary: An edit matching the finding's EDIT line for line settles its unit only when applied through apply-edits FROM=<reply>; an EDIT typed or copied by hand re-owes its unit. Appears in three places: Approach item 2 ('a unit changed any other way stays owed'), D43's 'Not built: settling an EDIT applied by hand', and D43's footer text ('an EDIT typed or copied by hand re-owes its unit').
decisions.why: The arbiter's ruling, which reached this review only as the dispatch's quote and not in the bundle, says: 'the modal-depiction re-owe guard should treat an edit whose diff matches, line for line, the verbatim EDIT the last round's finding supplied as settling that finding.' Its test is a property of the DIFF. D43 swaps that for a property of the MECHANISM. (1) Not impossible. D43's reason is 'the settling needs the reply's own blocks to tell a check's words from the session's'. That names an input the check needs, not something that cannot be done: apply-edits FROM=<reply or transcript> already takes that reply, and the same reply lets the check compare a working-tree diff with its EDIT blocks, however the edit reached the tree. If the plan's real premise is that the finding's EDIT text is kept nowhere the guard can read when the session edits by hand, that is a factual claim the block never measures, and scope cannot rest on it. (2) Not implied by the ruling: 'whose diff matches, line for line' read plainly covers any route an edit takes. (3) It defeats the ruling's purpose. Approach item 4 records that the T05 incident behind the ruling was hand-applied EDITs (page 0196's from a hand-made file, the pop-ups' by hand), so the carve-out leaves out the very case the ruling was written for, and the footer turns the carve-out into guidance that contradicts the ruling. Fix: the guard settles a unit when its working-tree diff matches, line for line, an EDIT in the last round's finding (the supplied reply or transcript), however the edit was applied; apply-edits FROM= stays one way to produce that match, not the only one that settles. Strike 'a unit changed any other way stays owed' from Approach item 2 (a unit whose diff departs from the EDIT stays owed) and the hand-edit sentence from the footer, and replace the 'Not built' sentence. An edit that departs from the EDIT, or one made with no reply to compare against, still re-owes.

decisions.summary: A tooling task found by T05: the claims gate refuses a MISLABELED claim already relabeled as prescribed, with no command to clear it.
decisions.why: Amendment 6, the GM verbatim: 'Please make sure to implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way.' A gate refusal nothing can clear is an obvious tooling defect; tooling only, one goal.

decisions.summary: claims.classify skips a MISLABELED finding whose current claim text differs from the text its verdict was recorded against while the unit body is the one judged; a relabel with the body moved stays owed and is judged again; a MISLABELED with unchanged text still refuses.
decisions.why: It is an exception to FR-013's last sentence ('a finding on ... a changed claim is still introduced and still refuses'). Legitimate on three grounds. (1) Purpose: FR-013 exists so a finding is fixed or re-checked clean before its feature closes; Approach step 4 records, dated 2026-10-18 with its method (make claims-owed, claims.py gate), that three claims relabeled as round 2's MISLABELED prescribed are not re-owed yet are refused, so the literal rule leaves a finding that is both fixed and unclearable, and the prescribed fix can never land. (2) The GM's own words: amendment 3 option 3, locked by the GM, 'Never block on unchanged code'; D45 requires the unit body unchanged. (3) Class check, each case on its own: the carve-out covers only MISLABELED with the body unchanged; a relabel with the body moved stays owed and judged, and a MISLABELED with unchanged text refuses as before, so FR-013's refusal of changed code survives whole. Premise the ruling rests on (not checkable from the bundle): the mechanism tests 'text differs', not 'text matches the prescription', and is defended as the same test feature 374's relabeled_only already applies on the owed side; the gate is brought into line with that existing rule, not given a new one.

decisions.why: A superset of the arbiter's trigger, not a carve-out from it: every claim the arbiter named still gets the inlining. Amendment 6 ('implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements') covers the widening, and the plan cites the evidence (T03's _clear_link, a link claim, hit the same CANNOT-TELL).

decisions.summary: Follows imported engine names and goes one call deeper from each callee found.
decisions.why: The arbiter's words: 'direct callees ... (transitively one level)'. The measured case (front_row then _front_row_from_chains / install_site_boundary) needs exactly that depth.

decisions.summary: A constant is an ALL_CAPS module-level name the unit or a callee reads, inlined as its assignment line with its comment.
decisions.why: An operational definition of the arbiter's word 'module-level constant' (the PEP 8 convention the codebase uses: HOUSE_PADDY_GAP_FT, STANDOFF_SLACK_PX), not a case taken out of it.

decisions.summary: A name outside l7r/ (standard library, third-party) is never followed.
decisions.why: Literally narrower than 'direct callees', but the fix states its purpose as ending 'asking for its call chain a round at a time', and every layer the three CANNOT-TELL rounds asked for (Approach item 4) was a project name; builtins and C extensions have no Python source to inline at all. The narrowing removes nothing the purpose needs.

decisions.summary: CALLEES_MAX rises from 6 to 12; past it the nearest first (the rest are dropped). Approach item 6: 'the cap is ours and stays'.
decisions.why: The arbiter's fix inlines 'direct callees and EVERY module-level constant they read (transitively one level)'. A cap that keeps the nearest 12 and drops the rest is not every, and a unit whose two depths and constants exceed 12 goes back to CANNOT-TELL and asks for the next layer, the exact failure the fix exists to end. The plan's own item 6 says the cap is ours, so keeping it is preserving existing behavior nobody asked to keep. It is not impossible to include everything (the depth is already bounded at two levels), and no arbiter or GM words in the bundle ask for a bound. D47 also does not say whether constants count toward the cap; either way something the ruling names is dropped. It would be within if nothing in the two depths is silently dropped, or at the very least if constants are never capped and an overflow is reported, not cut. Note too that done (item 9) names the six cross-module items but has not measured how many own-module callees _seat_households adds, so it has not shown the measured case fits in 12.

blocks: ## T25 - a claims bundle carries what the unit's code reads from other modules (the round arbiter's fix on ask:t05-old-drifts-at-landing)

decisions.summary: T25 lands open, on its own, with its retro row, before the next task starts.
decisions.why: FR-006 (one task, then the retro) and the GM's 'we do one task and then we measure' as written.

decisions.summary: For a claim whose label names a distance, gap or standoff (trigger words: distance, gap, standoff, apart, reach, clear of, off the, ft, feet), the bundle carries every engine function the unit calls, its own module's and imported, and every module constant it or they read, one level on, UNCAPPED.
decisions.why: On its words, this is the arbiter's tooling_fix as worded: 'direct callees and every module-level constant they read (transitively one level) whenever a claim's label names a distance, gap or standoff'. It is uncapped, so round 1's NOT LEGITIMATE cap of 12 is gone. The trigger carries the arbiter's three words literally and adds more distance words, which widens it. 'It or they' adds the unit's own constant reads, which also widens it. Its reach on the arbiter's motivating case is ruled separately (D47-reach).

decisions.summary: On the standoff claim on _seat_households, the arbiter's motivating case, the first bundle stops one hop down. HOUSE_PADDY_GAP_FT, read by _front_row_from_chains two calls below the unit, and install_site_boundary are reached only by (c), on a re-bundle after a first-round CANNOT-TELL. D47 justifies this with 'no fixed depth both fits a bundle and reaches it'.
decisions.why: The arbiter's fix states its purpose in the same sentence: 'so a standoff claim is judged in one round instead of asking for its call chain a round at a time'. By the blocks' own account, the claim the fix was written for still costs a CANNOT-TELL round. D47(c) says (c) reaches _front_row_from_chains, STANDOFF_SLACK_PX and HOUSE_PADDY_GAP_FT, 'the layer past one level', from a CANNOT-TELL note. That is fewer rounds, but still a round at a time on the named case. The impossibility premise is not measured and the blocks' own numbers contradict it: two levels of every callee is 82 KB, and the one-level bundle D47 accepts is 115 KB, so depth two is not shown not to fit. No bundle size limit is stated anywhere in the blocks. Under MODE 1 this is neither impossible nor implied by the words, and it defeats the fix's stated purpose on its own named case. The blocks also assert both outcomes at once: Approach item 1 ('judges a claim on the first round') and item 9 (the standoff unit's bundle carries install_site_boundary and HOUSE_PADDY_GAP_FT 'with no WITH=', quoted with (a)'s 115 KB / 63-entry figures) claim the first-round result that D47(a)'s 'one level on' and D47(c)'s 'layer past one level' say the first bundle does not deliver.

decisions.summary: Every claim's first bundle carries its own module's callees (at most CALLEES_MAX, 6, the existing t03 fix unchanged) plus every module constant the unit reads, imported ones too.
decisions.why: The callee cap is the arbiter's earlier fix (ask:t03-claims-at-landing) and is not changed here. Constants on every claim are an addition beside the arbiter's fix, covered by the GM's 'Please make sure to implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way' (amendment 6). For a distance claim (a) still applies uncapped, so (b)'s cap takes nothing from the arbiter's fix.

decisions.summary: A re-bundle of a claim last judged CANNOT-TELL chases each engine name its note backticks (resolved through imports, otherwise through at most three module-level definitions under l7r/), and walks breadth first through what those call or read, within CHASE_CHARS (30,000). The budget bounds only material past the arbiter's level.
decisions.why: This is an addition of ours past the arbiter's one level, under amendment 6's 'implement any obvious ... tooling improvements'. Its caps (three definitions, 30,000 characters) bound only our own addition: the block states that nothing in (a) is capped and that a chase stopping at the arbiter's level drops nothing from (a). It serves the arbiter's stated purpose ('judged in one round instead of asking for its call chain a round at a time') beyond what one level reaches.

decisions.summary: A name from outside l7r/ is never inlined or followed: (a)'s 'every engine function' and (c)'s chase reach only code under l7r/.
decisions.why: This is round 1's LEGITIMATE ruling, carried on the block's own wording. The arbiter's purpose is a bundle that keeps the judge from 'asking for its call chain a round at a time' on an engine claim, and that chain is the engine's code. Library and builtin calls, and tooling outside l7r/, are not what such a claim turns on (builtins written in C have no source to inline). The 'module-level constant' in the same sentence also refers to the engine's modules.

decisions.summary: The checklist part A answers: the goal is a first-round judgment; constraints and sources are labelled G or O; the measurement on T05 drove the design; budget 40 min; done is one goal with a test red without each of (a), (b), (c).
decisions.why: FR-003 (the Approach block) and FR-015 (one goal a task). Every addition is labelled as ours (O), not passed off as the arbiter's (G).

decisions.why: The arbiter's test is 'missing or older than its .gen.py or pool output'. Both renders (.png, .html) are checked, the .gen.py is checked, and the .json is the pool roll's output for a map (Approach item 4: make maps regenerated the pool and left renders missing). File times are the plain reading of 'older than' (labeled ours, O). If a pool roll writes any other per-map output a render depends on, it belongs in this list too - the arbiter said 'pool output', not '.json' - but nothing in the bundle names one.

decisions.why: The arbiter's fix is scoped to the renders verify 'snapshots and writes glyph-check prompts' for; a unit with no prompt owed has no glyph-check that could read a stale render.

decisions.why: Literally the arbiter's 'every unit whose render is missing' includes a Mode A sheet, so this narrows. Rendering it with make map GEN= is impossible (no generator), but the arbiter gave a second option, refusing - and the plan takes neither: a Mode A sheet is silently never listed, so if one can be owed with its .png or .html absent, a glyph-check runs on an absent render, which is exactly what the fix's purpose ('a glyph-check never runs on an absent or stale render') forbids. The plan states no reason, and nothing in the bundle establishes that a Mode A sheet's render cannot be absent or that it is never owed a glyph-check. Fix: list a Mode A sheet whose .png or .html is missing and refuse naming what restores it (only the 'older than its .gen.py' half has nothing to compare against), or keep the exclusion and state the measured premise that makes it a non-case (for example, that a Mode A sheet's render is tracked and a pool roll never removes it).

decisions.summary: Approach item 1 states the goal as a glyph OR settlement check reading a present, current render.
decisions.why: The behavior is the arbiter's alone: one render pass ahead of the snapshot. A settlement check reading the same snapshot benefits from it incidentally; no new behavior is added for it.

decisions.summary: One goal: review_snapshot.py --stale-renders names each owed map whose .png or .html is missing or older than its .gen.py or .json, make verify runs make map on each before the snapshot, and a test is red without it.
decisions.why: One goal per FR-015, stated as the arbiter's fix. The --stale-renders flag is the inspection surface for the same test; a test red without the fix is enforcement, not added scope.

decisions.why: The same rule already applied to T02-T26, which carries FR-006 (one task, then the retro). Adding the new task to that list decides nothing new.

decisions.summary: T24's Approach is re-stamped after its round-2 re-review. It keeps the goal, order, exit (c) and done-measure, adds round 2's constraint (the clone's history is left as it was when the patch applies), and answers item 4 afresh with the first real use: a real conflict on T26's landing refused with the merge aborted.
decisions.why: D9's third trigger and FR-003 ask for the Approach block to be answered again and stamped after the re-review. This block does that. 'Unchanged' is a real answer where nothing changed, and the item that could change (whether the constraints describe the world, item 4) is re-answered with new evidence. The added constraint narrows how the tooling acts, not what the GM asked for. The work itself is a tooling improvement under amendment 6.

decisions.summary: T27 is filed as its own task: a defect where the heading `owe` prints, stamped to the minute, is refused by `make tick` against a trigger time that carries seconds. It was found ticking T05 and T22.
decisions.why: Amendment 6 (the GM: 'Please make sure to implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way') covers it, and it is a tooling-only defect fix. It names one goal (FR-015). It was measured, not assumed: item 4 quotes the refusals of T05 (10:25:14Z vs 10:25Z) and T22 (09:33:15Z vs 09:33Z).

decisions.summary: approach_gate.refusal truncates the owed row's trigger time to the minute before comparing, so a block stamped in the trigger's own minute (the precision `owe` prints) passes, and a block stamped a minute earlier still refuses.
decisions.why: D9 says the owed block is 'stamped after the trigger'. Read to the second, a block stamped 10:25Z for a trigger at 10:25:14Z is before it, so D49 relaxes D9 within the trigger's own minute. Two of MODE 1's grounds apply. First, the literal rule cannot be met in the format the tool itself requires: the heading `owe` prints, and D9's own `### Txx part B (<UTC>)` form, carry minutes only. A block answered in the trigger's own minute, headed as instructed, can never pass. The session's only ways out would be to wait out the clock or stamp a false future minute. Second, the literal reading defeats D9's purpose (a fresh answer after the trigger, not one carried in from before) instead of serving it: the only extra blocks it lets through were written in the same sub-minute window, and a block from any earlier minute still refuses. The relaxation goes no further than the precision of the format the spec chose. It is one case, not several bundled together, and nothing in the GM's request asks for second-level precision. decisions.summary: 'A check that started and kept no reply stays counted, as the arbiter's "started an agent" allows.'
decisions.why: The fix says count ONLY dispatches that 'started an agent AND kept a reply'. A dispatch that started and kept no reply fails that test, so the fix says it is not counted. D56 counts it, and justifies that by quoting half of a two-part condition. That is completing the arbiter's thought for them. It also defeats the plan's own stated goal ('the cap counts readings, not attempts'), because a started agent with no reply is not a reading. Nothing makes the literal reading impossible. D56 must stop counting a started dispatch that kept no reply, or this carve-out must go to the arbiter.

decisions.summary: A refused dispatch is taken back only when a later dispatch finds it still 'pending' REFUSED_AFTER_S (60 s) after it was recorded. Until then it stays counted, including at a dispatch made within that minute.
decisions.why: The fix says refused dispatches 'should not count'. It names the pair hook's step-back block and 'any other refusal before launch', and asks for 'a test where a refused dispatch leaves the count unchanged'. Under D56, a session that dispatches again within 60 s of a refusal (the likely response to a step-back block) is charged a round for the refused dispatch at that next dispatch. The cap can then fire on readings that never happened, which is the incident's failure. The plan's own Done line ('a dispatch never launched is taken back at the next dispatch') is false in that case. The window is the plan's own choice (Approach item 3 marks it O), and its reason is that one hook cannot see another hook's refusal. That makes this mechanism awkward. Also unmeasured: the premise that 'the launch's PostToolUse follows in seconds'. Approach item 4 measures only the incident. If a foreground dispatch's PostToolUse comes when the agent finishes, a reading in flight for more than 60 s would be taken back, contradicting D56's 'a launched dispatch is never taken back'.

decisions.id: T70-A2 Stop guard, not a cron

decisions.summary: Of the approved proposal's three escapes, the second (a turn ending with a question to the GM) is dropped; a turn that really waits on the GM must set the feature down with WHY="awaiting the GM on <what>".
decisions.why: This departs from the proposal the GM approved, so it gets a ruling. It meets two of the tests. (1) It is implied by the GM's own words: the request names exactly two acceptable states, 'either still in progress or has been correctly set down', and a turn ending in a question is neither. (2) Keeping the escape would defeat the request's stated purpose, 'stopping with tasks partially done is a constant problem'. The motivating case is the overnight run of amendment 6, where a turn ending 'Shall I go on to the next task?' while the GM sleeps is exactly the stall the guard exists to stop, and nothing in a Stop hook can tell a rhetorical question from a real one. Nothing the GM relies on is taken away: a turn that really waits on him stays reachable through a recorded set-down that names what it waits for (Approach step 2), which makes it more visible to him, not less.

decisions.summary: The guard never holds a turn while a background command or agent started in the session has not reported back.
decisions.why: This is the approved proposal's first escape ('something is still running that will wake the session (a background gate, an agent)'). The proposal's safety net for a hung job is the existing 90-minute ceiling, which is unchanged.

decisions.why: The GM asked for this 'when a feature is begun'. task-start is the moment a feature's work begins, and a clone with no task-start has no feature begun.

decisions.id: T70 D89 GM-review box excluded from 'open task'
decisions.summary: A feature counts as in progress when its tasks.md has an open box other than the GM-review box and its status line does not close it.
decisions.why: This narrows what counts as 'in progress'. Applied literally, the rule would defeat its own purpose. The GM-review box is the GM's own step, not one the session can work. If that box is the only one open, the feature has nothing left for the session to do, so it is not 'still in progress' in the sense of the GM's words. Holding the turn would demand work that does not exist and would make the session invent work or set the feature down without cause. A feature whose status line closes it is likewise not in progress. Each other open task is still caught.

decisions.why: This is a carve-out the GM never mentioned: the guard is silent exactly when it cannot decide. It is legitimate because failing closed would defeat the purpose and could leave no reachable exit. If the guard cannot read task-starts.jsonl, tasks.md or set-downs.jsonl, then make set-down, the only escape it offers, may itself fail to satisfy it. A Stop hook that refuses every turn end in that state holds the session in a loop that neither the GM's 'in progress' nor his 'set down' describes. Each fail-open is recorded in the guard log, so the GM can see every silent turn. It is not a quiet exemption.

decisions.summary: Farmsteads carved within the paddy proposed to the GM as a feature of its own, first settling 0017's 1.3 acres and the 205-273 ft width
decisions.why: The arbiter's ruling. It is proposed, not filed, which respects feature 377's rule that features are filed only with the GM's approval.

decisions.summary: T05's standoff claim judged on the 6 ft floor only (10-13 ft treated as a drawn figure, not a maximum); the row village's whole-farmstead standoff left UNCLAIMED
decisions.why: Carried by the round arbiter (ask:t05-old-drifts-at-landing). That attribution comes from the dispatch, and the bundle does not show whether the arbiter ruled on this reading or only moved the claim. Whether 10-13 ft is a maximum is a research-ladder question, not a fidelity one. Nothing in T06 widens or narrows the claim.

decisions.summary: One goal: cohort 54/54, each dispersed seed in single file (all households, no rank) or as at HEAD
decisions.why: One goal, as FR-015 requires, and matches the arbiter's 'cohort 54/54'. Step 9's wording is inverted: it says 'seeds whose line holds' are filed as the gap, while D52 files the seeds in ranks. This is a drafting error to fix before Done is measured, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: A research-pass agent searches the archive then the web (Chinese, Japanese, English) for a village house's wall/eaves-to-lane clearance (eaves-drip strip, set-back, building line); an attested figure enters the record and TREAD_WALL_FT moves to it (pool and cohort rolled); none found, the claim reads UNRESEARCHED naming the pass and 4 ft stays.
decisions.why: The ranking row itself reads 'research the clearance or claim it UNRESEARCHED'; D55 is exactly those two outcomes, in that order. Keeping 4 ft under an UNRESEARCHED label is the row's own second branch, and nothing in the task forces the knob to move. The request asks for about five ranking rows of different kinds, and this is a research-first one.

decisions.summary: Exits (a) refine the number and (e) conform the label apply; (b) exception, (c) new rule, (d) more room are n/a.
decisions.why: No rule is being worked against here. The task is a sourcing question on one constant, so exception, new-rule and more-room exits have nothing to act on. Judging them n/a answers the checklist (FR-003) and does not narrow the row.

decisions.summary: China first, Japan as the tiebreaker; one search pass, a second only on a lead the first names.
decisions.why: The research rules the plan cites set the source order and the search-before-guess discipline. A one-pass limit with a lead-driven second pass decides how much effort the research gets. It does not drop any part of what the row asks for, which is to research the clearance or label it UNRESEARCHED.

decisions.summary: 60 min budget; one goal: TREAD_WALL_FT's claim cites the pass's finding or reads UNRESEARCHED with the pass named, and the ranking row is marked with its wave.
decisions.why: The per-task budget and the single goal are the measured, one-task-at-a-time process the GM asked for (FR-006, FR-015). The done condition is the ranking row's own two outcomes.

decisions.summary: The hourly step-back's arbiter reads what every session working the feature said and did in the hour, not only the busiest session's.
decisions.why: It restates the arbiter's fix (G), and that fix is tooling the GM asked for in amendment 6 ('implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'). The arbiter stands where the GM was asked (feature 379). Measured case: the window held three sessions and words.md carried only one.

decisions.summary: The constraint is the arbiter's fix, quoted: words from every session transcript active in the hour, keeping the newest, listing any transcript left out or cut.
decisions.why: The fix is carried as written and nothing in it is narrowed. Being an arbiter's fix, its full text is outside request.md and this bundle (the quote is elided at '...'), so its content was not re-verified against the arbiter's ruling here.

decisions.summary: The replay flags (--transcript, SC-008) stay unchanged.
decisions.why: This keeps an accepted success criterion (SC-008, amendment 4's replay of T03) working. It does not keep any behavior the fix asks to change: the fix is about which transcripts the hourly bundle reads, not the replay path.

decisions.summary: Tooling only; a test in tests/tooling/test_checkpoint.py that is red without the change.
decisions.why: Tooling only matches the fix's scope. The test only fails when the requested behavior is missing, so it enforces the request and is not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: The order is sessions, then words, refusals and time over them, then tests. Exit (c) is taken (a rule that removes the case: read every session, not the busiest). The budget is 40 min.
decisions.why: These are execution choices inside the fix and the checklist's own fields (FR-003). None of them changes what is delivered.

decisions.summary: Done means that, on an hour of two sessions, the bundle carries both sessions' words, each labeled, and names a session whose transcript it could not find.
decisions.why: One goal, as FR-015 requires. Labeling each session's words is what 'from every session' needs to be readable, so it adds nothing. The done check tests 'left out' but does not separately test 'keeping the newest' or listing a transcript it 'cut'. Those stay binding through constraint 2, so this is not a narrowing. It is a gap the test would ideally cover: see the aside.

decisions.summary: New `make claims-carry F= KEYS= RULING= [T=]` form files findings the gate counts as introduced, which a round-arbiter ruling carried, into a named open task or a new box, and writes a claims-carried.jsonl row; `holding` honors the box by its id from that row (D28 unchanged).
decisions.why: Broadens rather than narrows: it applies FR-013/D28's filed-box rule (amendment 3 option 3, 'the gate files the finding as an open task... automates what the arbiter did by hand') to boxes an arbiter ruling carried, and is a tooling improvement amendment 6 authorizes ('implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'). The filed box is still an open task, so the feature cannot close until the finding is fixed - the property option 3 keeps. Labeled honestly as ours (O).

decisions.summary: A RULING that is not a `trigger` in the feature's arbiter.jsonl is refused.
decisions.why: Tightens the new command to recorded arbiter rulings only; narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: A hand-typed [lands-open] box, even one citing a recorded trigger, still holds the landing; only the box the command writes with its record is honored.
decisions.why: Keeps D28's rule ('the tooling put it there, as the open-task rule requires') intact; the earlier form that let a trigger-naming hand mark through was the one round 1 blocked.

decisions.summary: The push's claims gate is unchanged: an introduced finding still needs CLAIMS_OK citing the ruling.
decisions.why: Matches FR-013's 'a finding on changed code or a changed claim is still introduced and still refuses, as before'; the plan touches only the open-task hold, not the introduced-finding refusal.

decisions.summary: T43 is filed through the new command (T=T43) and its id comes off the plan's Lands open line at T45's next plan edit.
decisions.why: Applies the decision to the case that motivated it; drops a hand-typed workaround, not a requirement.

decisions.summary: tests/tooling/test_lands_open.py made red without the change.
decisions.why: A test that only fails when the decided behavior is absent; enforcement, not added scope.

decisions.summary: POND_BANKS knob (bare, planted) rolled per hamlet at even odds (GUESS), HamletSpec override, meta.pond_bank; only a pond sink rolls it
decisions.why: Unchanged since its CLEAR verdict; the ranking row asks for exactly this knob, rolled from the seed per the knob rule.

decisions.summary: stage_pond_bank after stage_lane_wells, before stage_hinterland; seats walked at a GUESS pitch round the fringe's outer edge plus half a crown, each kept only where clear of buildings, wells, ways, crop and water
decisions.why: Unchanged since its CLEAR verdict; draws the planted form's trees, seated after houses and ways, forced onto nothing.

decisions.summary: For every tail pond, bare or planted, the bank's ellipse (pond radii + SINK_FRINGE + POND_BANK_FT 18 ft GUESS) joins block_polys so the toe marsh and scatters stay off the bank; each tree jittered across the bank within the 6 ft the crown leaves

It covers bare banks too, and that is not extra scope: the bare form the knob rolls is 0061's trodden or mown bank, not marsh, so keeping it dry is part of drawing both rolled forms faithfully. The new numbers are labeled GUESS knobs. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The bank tree is held to thin_planted_trees' sun rule at seating rather than through _plant_run (which writes only planted_trees, unread by structures_clear_of_trees); crown recorded in tree_crowns; kinds in pond_bank_trees; the bank mulberry read as 0061's shade tree for cattle, not 0038's exempt field bush
decisions.why: Part A's sun-rule constraint (0038) is kept, and the structure-overlap test is now actually reached. This changes how the rule is applied, not what it covers; nothing is exempted.

decisions.summary: 0061's 'not drawn yet' bullet rewritten to the knob's own, GUESSes labeled, by a page session
decisions.why: Unchanged since its CLEAR verdict; the record line a new element owes.

decisions.summary: Four older _OVERLAP_EXEMPT drifts re-opened by the one added key carried into T43, landing under CLAIMS_OK on ask:t08-overlap-exempt-drifts (continue); per-entry keying of the claims record left to the GM's review
decisions.why: This is the GM's amendment 3 option three: a finding on unchanged code is filed as an open task and does not block the landing. Not starting an overhaul of the claims record that nobody asked for narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Re-answered Approach: goal now includes the bank standing dry; done = no toe-marsh inside any bank ellipse and no bank trunk in any marsh, on pool and cohort, glyph check passing; 90 min budget; bank width a knob band
decisions.why: One goal still: the two attested bank forms drawn faithfully. The added done-conditions are the measurable test of D61b and of Part A's 0061 constraint, which is enforcement of what was asked, not a second goal (FR-015).

decisions.summary: With Makefile in FILES, land-tooling runs the make-docs check in the clone before building the patch; a stale clone page is refused naming `make docs`; a current page that differs from main's is added to FILES; the worktree's own regeneration stays.
decisions.why: This is the arbiter's fix, which stands where the GM was asked (feature 379): 'runs make docs and lands the regenerated make-targets page together with a changed Makefile, refusing to land when the page would be stale'. D64 does each part. The refusal is the arbiter's own named refusal, and it reaches only the Makefile case. Landing the page beside the Makefile is the 'lands ... together'. The worktree regeneration that is kept is the 'runs make docs'. It also serves Amendment 5 item 1 (check the page whenever the Makefile changes, approved as 'file amendment 5 for the 3 tooling fixes'), FR-017, and Amendment 6's 'implement any obvious ... tooling ... improvements'. Nothing is excepted or narrowed.

decisions.summary: The check command can be overridden through LAND_TOOLING_DOCS_CHECK (default `python3 scripts/make-docs.py . --check`).
decisions.why: This is a test seam for the arbiter's required tests/hooks test, which is 'red without each'. The default runs the real check. It adds no behavior and changes no scope.

decisions.summary: One goal: refuse while the clone's page is stale, land the page when it is current; tests/hooks/test-land-tooling.sh red without each.
decisions.why: The goal is single (FR-015) and the test is the one the arbiter asked for. The test only enforces the requested behavior, so it serves the request (GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: T04 to T10 carry T48, T47's patch and five ranking rows, one task each
decisions.why: The approved proposal's scope lists exactly these after the lane law and the four seeds: 'T48', 'T47's patch re-landed', 'about five ranking rows of different kinds'; FR-007 moves them here. Seven items over seven tasks narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Taken in the order T48, T47's patch, then the ranking rows
decisions.why: The proposal says the items are 'taken in the order 384's "How it starts" already sets' and lists them in this order; FR-007 cites the same moved work.

decisions.id: decided at start via make decide
decisions.summary: Each task's section is decided at its own start, added to the plan and reviewed by make decide
decisions.why: The proposal hooks the checklist into 'the existing make task-start / make decide step' before the first edit, and FR-007 says the ranking rows are 'chosen at the start of their task'. Deferring each section to its task start is what was asked, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: The remaining moved items are T48, T47's patch and five ranking rows, one task each (T04 to T10).
decisions.why: The approved proposal's scope lists exactly these after the lane law and the four seeds: T48, T47's patch re-landed, about five ranking rows; FR-007 moves T48 and T47 here.

decisions.summary: Taken in the order T48, T47's patch, then the ranking rows.
decisions.why: The proposal says the items are taken in the order 384's How it starts sets, listed as lane law, seeds, T48, T47's patch, ranking rows; the block keeps that order.

decisions.summary: Each task decided at its start, its plan section added then and reviewed by make decide.
decisions.why: FR-007: ranking rows chosen at the start of their task; FR-003: each task's plan section carries an Approach block; the proposal hooks the checklist into make task-start / make decide.

decisions.summary: approach_gate.py's part-B reader compares each '### Tnn part B (<stamp>)' stamp, truncated to the minute per T27's rule, with the current UTC minute and refuses a later one, naming the stamp and the clock; make plan-delta asks the same reader so both gates refuse it.
decisions.why: Enforcement of D9/FR-004 (a part B 'stamped after the trigger'): a stamp later than the clock satisfies the after-the-trigger comparison without being written after it, so the refusal makes the requested rule actually hold. It is the arbiter's fix as worded (both the tick's check and make plan-delta, with a test), leaves T27's minute rule unchanged, and reaches no other command or agent; it also falls under the GM's amendment 6 ('implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way').

decisions.summary: Tooling only: the rule in approach_gate.py, then a test in tests/tooling/test_approach_gate.py red without it; one goal.
decisions.why: Exactly the arbiter's fix (rule plus a test that a future-stamped part B is refused and a present one passes), one goal per FR-015; the test only fails when the requested refusal is absent, so it is verification of the request, not added scope.

decisions.summary: The Makefile's tree-check abort records `failed-gate tree-moved` instead of `failed-gate done`; ci/state.py already counts only `done` toward red-in-a-row, so no engine change; the failed record still overwrites the green slot.
decisions.why: The first half of the arbiter's fix, as the block quotes it: a tree-moved abort is not counted as a red make done. Keeping the green slot overwritten preserves FR-004/FR-010's rule that nothing vouches for a moved tree. The arbiter's words are quoted inside the block rather than supplied in request.md; taken as quoted under feature 379, and the Approach's request.md basis is amendment 6 ('implement any obvious ... tooling / process improvements').

decisions.summary: arbiter_bundle.red_gate_runs passes over a run whose result is 'failed: tree moved'.
decisions.why: The same half of the arbiter's fix applied to the bundle: a tree-moved abort is not among the counted reds the arbiter is shown.

decisions.summary: Between each pair of listed reds, the bundle carries the full `git diff <earlier> <later>` between their recorded commits, with its --stat as a header.
decisions.why: The second half of the arbiter's fix, 'the diff between each pair of counted reds'. This replaces the earlier text's --stat-only version, which fell short of 'the diff', and moves toward the arbiter's words rather than away from them. The Done line (Approach item 9) was updated to match.

decisions.summary: Two reds on one commit are reported as 'the same commit; uncommitted edits between them are not recorded' rather than as an empty diff.
decisions.why: This does not exclude a case from the rule. It labels what the rule produces: between identical recorded commits the diff is empty, and the clause states that and says what the record cannot show. Nothing the arbiter asked the bundle to carry is withheld. Reading the fix as also requiring the gate to start recording working-tree state would be completing the arbiter's thought. The premise 'a run record keeps its commit and no tree state' is the plan's statement and was not measured in this review, because the bundle allows no repository reads.

decisions.summary: Tooling only; order: abort record, then bundle filter and diffs, then tests; exit (c); 40 min budget; one goal, with a test red without each half.
decisions.why: Sequencing, budget and the testing obligation decide nothing the arbiter's fix or 375's FR-004/FR-010 left open in a narrowing direction. A test red without each half enforces the requested fix.

decisions.summary: An autouse fixture in tests/tooling/test_plan_gate.py points plan_bundle.OUT at each test's tmp_path, so no two tests (decide_prompt's test and test_the_decide_commands) share a bundle path under /tmp/l7r-check.
decisions.why: A test-isolation fix to a race measured on T08's gate (FileNotFoundError on /tmp/l7r-check/plan-375-x-T05, passing alone). It is a tooling fix found along the way, which amendment 6 asks for verbatim ('Please make sure to implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'). It changes only where the tests write; no requested behavior is altered or narrowed.

decisions.summary: Session-dispatched bundles stay at /tmp/l7r-check; only the tests move theirs; tooling only.
decisions.why: Keeps existing behavior the request never asked to change and confines the fix to the defect; it removes nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: The formatter's sorting of T49's test imports, seen on the same gate, is left to T49 and re-lands with T49 rather than being fixed here.
decisions.why: Not a narrowing of any request: the defect is still fixed, in the task that owns it. Keeping it out of T51 follows FR-015 (one goal a task), which the GM approved in amendment 4 ('a second goal becomes its own task').

decisions.summary: land-tooling's checks step runs ruff check and ruff format --check on the .py files among FILES, in the landing's worktree; a failure is a failing check, so nothing lands, and the message names the files and the fix (ruff format <file> or the rule)
decisions.why: Amendment 6 (GM 2026-10-18, verbatim): 'Please make sure to implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way.' Measured 2026-10-18 per the Approach: T49's and T51's landings put unformatted Python on main, caught only by the next make done. Applying the gate's own existing lint/format rules (constitution: ruff, ruff format) at landing is an obvious tooling fix; it adds no new rule, only moves an existing check earlier. Limiting it to .py files and to the landed files is the extent of the gap found, not a cut to anything the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: LAND_TOOLING_LINT environment variable, defaulting to the two ruff commands, as a seam for tests/hooks/test-land-tooling.sh
decisions.why: A test seam whose default is the requested check; it exists only so the red-without-it test can run. It enforces the improvement and does not change behavior for anyone who leaves it at its default.

decisions.summary: Tooling only; one goal (refuse a landed Python file failing ruff check or ruff format --check); test red without it
decisions.why: Matches FR-015's one-goal rule and SC-style red-without-it testing; adds nothing the request did not authorize under amendment 6.

decisions.summary: land-tooling (and so arbiter-fix-done, which lands through it) runs ledger_owed.py --refuse before its worktree and before any timed check, refusing at once with the owed rows
decisions.why: This is the arbiter's fix as quoted in the Approach (the arbiter stands where the GM was asked, feature 379), and it is the kind of obvious tooling improvement the GM asked for in amendment 6. 'Before its worktree' falls inside 'before it starts its timed checks'.

decisions.summary: the push's own ledger check is kept; the early check is added in front of it
decisions.why: The fix moves when the refusal is felt and does not repeal the rule. Keeping the push's check (385 FR-019's refusal) removes nothing anyone asked for.

decisions.summary: the early check reads the ledger as committed at HEAD, which is what the landing carries, through a LAND_TOOLING_LEDGER seam for the test
decisions.why: Checking what will land is what makes the early refusal agree with the push it replaces in time. The seam is there only so the requested test can be red without the check. That is enforcement of the request, not added scope.

decisions.summary: the refusal names the owed rows and the command `make ledger-owed WRITE=...`
decisions.why: The fix says 'naming the owed rows', and 385 FR-019 has every ledger refusal name the command that writes the rows.

decisions.summary: LEDGER_ROWS_OK waives the early check as it already waives the push's
decisions.why: Read literally, 'refuses at once' has no waiver, so this carves out a case. But the fix's own words imply it: the refusal comes 'instead of after the checks have run, at the push', so it moves the push's refusal earlier. Where the push would not refuse (waiver set), an early refusal would be a new block the fix never asked for and would defeat its purpose of refusing earlier only what will be refused anyway. One case, one argument; no seam.

decisions.summary: tests/hooks/test-land-tooling.sh is red without the early check
decisions.why: The fix asks for a test red without the change (and 385 SC-009 asks for the same). The test only checks that the requested refusal happens.

decisions.summary: plan_gate.active_task honors .git/active-task only while its task's box is open; a mark naming a ticked or missing task falls back to the first open task, as when there is no mark.
decisions.why: FR-004 / D9 (the GM's 'a checklist ... that comes up when a session is taking a while', enforced by make tick) only works if an owed part B lands on a task that can still be ticked; a part B owed by a ticked task is unenforceable. The fallback restores the enforcement the GM asked for and does not narrow it: it adds no trigger, removes none, and changes no floor. 'First open task' matches FR-006 (tasks run one at a time, in order). The session's own make task-start mark still wins while its task is open, so nothing the session chose is overridden. Covered also by amendment 6 ('implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way').

decisions.summary: Every reader of the active task (approach-gate triggers and 375's decide-first guards) gets the same fallback answer.
decisions.why: With a stale mark, a decide-first guard read the ticked task, whose decisions already stood, so it passed on work belonging to the next task - a gap in the guard, not a scope. Giving every reader the same answer closes that gap; it adds no refusal of a new kind and widens no reach beyond the work the guards already cover, and FR-003a's rule is unchanged as the constraints state.

decisions.summary: Tooling only; FR-003a and D9 unchanged; a test in tests/tooling/test_plan_gate.py red without the fallback; budget 20 min; exit (c).
decisions.why: The test only fails when the requested enforcement (FR-004's owed block landing on a live task) is absent, so it enforces the request (SC-004: refusals of FR-003 and FR-004 each have a test red without them). Nothing in the constraints narrows a requirement.

decisions.summary: T52's two ruff commands (check and format) in make land-tooling carry --force-exclude, so pyproject.toml's extend-exclude holds for the files a landing names explicitly, as it does for the gate's own `ruff check .`.
decisions.why: Amendment 6 asks the session to 'implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'; T52's landing lint is session tooling under that clause, and this decision repairs a defect in it rather than narrowing anything the GM asked. It does not loosen T52's stated purpose (no landed file fails the gate's lint): the gate does not lint excluded paths, so linting them on a landing refused work the gate would pass (the measured case, T54's fix to scripts/gates/plan_gate.py). The included-file case is still refused, and a test red without the flag is in the Done line. No GM clause and no FR (FR-017/FR-018/FR-019 included) is narrowed.

decisions.summary: BUNDLE_PITCH keeps 100 ft; its claim is conformed from 'row pitch - 0038' (MISLABELED) to 'the along-row span - UNRESEARCHED', naming stages._rank_step (envelope depth + max(lane room, SUN_CORRIDOR_FT 39 ft)) as the row-to-row step that carries 0038's 92 ft; comments calling it the row pitch or a homestead's ground are corrected; no map changes
decisions.why: The GM asked for ranking rows (claims) to be taken so the code matches the research (request: 'about five ranking rows', amendment 7 'pull in 10 more claims'). The research figure is 0038's rows 92 ft apart; the plan says the row-to-row step is already _rank_step (house + yard + 39 ft sun, about 93 ft per 0038's own words) and that BUNDLE_PITCH is the along-row and grid span, so the research is met and the defect is the label. The ranking row's '100 -> 92' prescription is the ranking's own suggested fix, not the GM's words; the plan's measurement (2026-10-18, BUNDLE_PITCH at 92: rows unchanged, cohort 52/54 with seeds 17 and 43 regressing) shows that prescription would not move the rows at all, so following it would not serve the purpose. Choosing 'conform the label' among named exits is what the GM-approved checklist asks for, and recording BUNDLE_PITCH honestly as UNRESEARCHED narrows nothing the GM asked. The ranking row's re-derive of HOMESTEAD_GROUND_FT and WEB_REACH_FT ties is consequential on a number move that does not happen; the plan still states each one's source (WEB_REACH_FT 0246, HOMESTEAD_GROUND_FT UNRESEARCHED).

decisions.summary: The three splits recorded as water shares (0.6, 0.4, 0.7) - 6:4 water, 6:4 dike, 7:3 water.
decisions.why: Exactly the three splits the ranking row names (water-heavy, dike-heavy, 7:3), sourced to 0018.

decisions.summary: The split rolled per map from its seed as a settlement knob `dikepond_split`, pinnable by a hamlet spec.
decisions.why: The row asks for the inset rolled per village; a seed-rolled knob is the project's standing form for several attested forms. Per map is per village here (one village a map).

decisions.summary: Even odds between the three splits, labeled GUESS.
decisions.why: The row says roll between the splits and gives no weights; even odds labeled GUESS settles an open detail without excluding any split.

decisions.summary: The inset derived once per map from the rolled share on the map's median parcel by the rectangle law, stored on the settlement.
decisions.why: Implements the inset as the rolled split's value on the map's own parcels; done is measured on all its parcels (within a few points), so no split or parcel is excused.

decisions.summary: Every reader of the inset (pond water outline, mulberry rows, sties' bank seat at half the inset) reads the one stored value.
decisions.why: Keeps the readers consistent with the rolled split; without it the roll would reach only the water outline.

decisions.summary: DIKEPOND_WATER_INSET (23 ft) kept, labeled as the water-heavy split's value on Kuwabata, as the fallback where no parcel is known.
decisions.why: A fallback for the no-parcel case only; every map with parcels takes the derived inset of its rolled split, so it narrows nothing the row asks.

decisions.summary: 0018's drawing page known-gap sentence rewritten to the knob, by a page session.
decisions.why: The gap the page names is the one this row closes; bringing the page up to the code keeps the record true.

decisions.summary: task_sections first gives each id the first heading whose title BEGINS with that id (## T10 - ..., ### T10 Approach); only an id no heading begins with falls back to the first heading that mentions it, as before.
decisions.why: A tooling fix so a task's decision preflight reviews that task's own section rather than an umbrella heading that only names it - the per-task check the GM approved (request: the checklist asked at task start 'enforced by the existing decide/tick tooling', and amendment 6 'implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'). It removes a measured defect (T47/T48/T10 preflights reviewed the umbrella heading) without narrowing anything the request or spec asks; the fallback keeps every plan already written resolving as before.

decisions.summary: Tooling only, plans already written keep their headings, one goal, a test in tests/tooling/test_plan_gate.py red without the rule.
decisions.why: One goal per task is FR-015 (amendment 4); the test only fails when the requested behavior is absent, so it is enforcement of the fix, not added scope; leaving existing plans' headings untouched narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: A comment- or docstring-only change to engine Python owes neither a full make done nor a landing cohort; the fix goes in the one definition (gate-stamp.py semantic_bytes, loaded by ci/delta.py) that both the green-gate guard and sync-with-main.sh's cohort requirement read.
decisions.why: It is the arbiter's fix restated (the arbiter stands where the GM was asked, feature 379), and it is the obvious tooling improvement that Amendment 6 asked for along the way. Putting it in the single shared definition reaches both mechanisms the fix names and nothing else. Nothing the fix covers is left out.

decisions.summary: semantic_bytes removes every bare string-constant statement from every statement list, not only a body's first statement; an emptied body dumps as an empty list.
decisions.why: The fix's purpose is that a change touching no code that runs owes no engine gate, and its named case is a constant's claim docstring, which Python does not treat as a docstring because it is not the first statement. Stripping only first statements would leave that exact case unfixed (the measured T09 incident). A bare Constant string is evaluated and thrown away, so the constraint that every token that runs still moves the key holds. f-strings are JoinedStr nodes, not bare constants, so they stay in the id. This widens what counts as non-engine only to strings that do not execute, which is what the fix is for. It does not narrow it.

decisions.summary: The semantic-id cache file is renamed to semantic-id-cache-2.json, so every engine key moves once and each session's next gate re-runs once.
decisions.why: Implementation hygiene so that ids computed by the old rule are not reused. It is a one-time cost of applying the fix and drops nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: Done is one goal: two module versions differing only in a constant's claim docstring and a comment share one semantic id and a changed value does not; tests/tooling/test_gate_stamp* is red without it.
decisions.why: The fix asks for a test that is red without it. This test only fails when the requested behavior is missing, so it enforces the fix. The changed-value half checks the fix's own constraint that code which runs still moves the key.

decisions.summary: Order (rule, cache name, test), exit (c), no search smell, 30-minute budget.
decisions.why: Process fields of the checklist (FR-003). They narrow nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: In agent-prefix-hooks.sh's wave refusal, a session carrying L7R_DISPATCHER is told it has no Workflow tool and to put WAVE_OK: <reason> in each prompt of the batch, and is not shown the check-wave call; an interactive session's message is unchanged.
decisions.why: This is the arbiter's fix as worded (name WAVE_OK as the route when the session has no Workflow tool, instead of pointing a headless session at a tool it lacks). The arbiter stands where the GM was asked (feature 379), and the GM's amendment 6 asks for obvious tooling and process improvements along the way. Leaving the interactive message unchanged keeps the existing behavior the fix did not ask to change. Nothing is carved out.

decisions.summary: 'The session has no Workflow tool' is detected by L7R_DISPATCHER being set (queued headless page sessions carry it; interactive ones do not).
decisions.why: This is the mechanism for the fix's own condition, not a narrowing of it. The fix's stated object is a headless session pointed at a tool it lacks, and Approach item 4 records as measured (2026-10-18, page_session_runner.headless_env) that queued headless sessions carry the variable. The incident that prompted the fix was such a session (T10's check session at 19:48).

decisions.summary: tests/hooks/test-agent-prefix-hooks.sh gains a case that is red without the branch: with L7R_DISPATCHER the refusal names WAVE_OK and no Workflow call; without it, the message is as before.
decisions.why: The test enforces exactly what was asked, and its only effect is that the requested refusal text happens and keeps happening. That is enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope. The fix itself names 'a test red without it' as part of the work.

decisions.summary: hm_checks keeps what a dispatch's reading would mark (seen sentences, notes read, the fresh round's edits reset) on its pending record and applies it only in launched(), when an agent id returns; a dispatch refused before launch changes nothing but its own pending record, which expires via _live and counts no round.
decisions.why: This is how the plan carries out the arbiter's fix (the arbiter stands where the GM was asked, feature 379; amendment 6 also asks for obvious tooling/process fixes along the way). It reaches the fix's stated purpose, that a refused dispatch cannot push a unit to its round cap, because the marks that made the next real dispatch count as a later round are never applied. It covers a refusal by any hook, not only the wave guard. That is wider than the fix names, not narrower, and adds no new refusing or blocking behavior. T41's reply rule is left unchanged, as the constraints require. The fix's 'or keep as a pending round' clause is met because the pending record counts no round, and the Done measure checks this: the next dispatch of the same unit must be a first look.

decisions.summary: tests/tooling/test_hm_checks.py: a recorded-but-never-launched dispatch leaves seen, notes_read and the round's edits unchanged, and the next dispatch of the unit is a first look; red without the fix.
decisions.why: Its only job is to enforce the arbiter's fix and the task's single goal. It is verification of the requested behavior, not added scope.

decisions.summary: T60 is a tooling-only task: apply_edits.py takes an EDIT whose new text is a paragraph break, and drops a line an empty replacement empties, each with a test in tests/tooling/test_apply_edits.py red without it; every other EDIT applies as before.
decisions.why: The GM's amendment 6 (2026-10-18) asks the session to 'implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'; the task carries the arbiter's fix part 1 as quoted, no wider, and was measured (two hand finishes in T10's check session). The tests only fail when the requested behavior is absent, so they enforce the fix rather than add scope.

decisions.summary: A block whose new text is exactly one empty line replaces its old text with a paragraph break (\n\n inside a line, a blank line between lines); a block whose new text is empty and whose old text was the whole of its line removes the line and its newline; every other block applies as before.
decisions.why: This is the arbiter's fix stated as a parse rule: 'a bare paragraph break' read as a lone empty line between === and >>>, and 'the line an empty replacement empties' read as an empty replacement of a line's whole text. Neither reading excludes a case the fix names, and 'every other block applies as before' preserves only what the fix did not ask to change.

decisions.summary: Order: the parse, the empty-line drop, then their tests; exit (c); budget 30 min; one goal.
decisions.why: Sequencing and a time budget inside the requested work; the one-goal 'done' follows FR-015 (amendment 4).

decisions.summary: hm_make.classify returns make-dup-var when one make invocation assigns one variable name twice; make-only-hooks.sh refuses it, naming the variable and the two compliant forms (quoted list, or one call per value).
decisions.why: This is the arbiter's fix part 2 as quoted in the Approach (a Bash guard refusing a make call that assigns a variable twice, naming Q="a b" or one call per value); feature 379 has the arbiter's ruling stand where the GM was asked, and amendment 6 directs obvious tooling/process improvements along the way. The refusal reaches exactly the case the fix names and no other command or agent type.

decisions.summary: Quotes and heredocs are stripped before counting assignments, as the guard already strips them.
decisions.why: Implements the fix's own carve-in that a quoted list passes (Q="0018 0027" is one assignment); reuses the guard's existing parse rather than adding a new scope.

decisions.summary: make x Q="a b" and make x Q=a R=b pass.
decisions.why: Both are stated by the arbiter's fix (the quoted-list form is the named compliant form; distinct variables are a different case from a doubled assignment).

decisions.summary: The escape is the guard's existing GUARD_EDIT_OK, recorded.
decisions.why: Not a carve-out of any case: no class of doubled assignment is exempted by rule, and the override is the existing, recorded escape every refusal in this guard already carries. It adds no new mechanism or default.

decisions.summary: tests/hooks/test-make-only-hooks.sh carries a test red without the refusal.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested refusal (the fix itself says a test red without it); if the refusal is deleted the test has nothing left to check.

decisions.summary: A task is added by one command, make task-add, that picks the id and places the box and plan section; tooling only, with a test that fails without it.
decisions.why: Amendment 8, verbatim: 'do we need some tooling around how to insert a task ... somewhere in the middle of the task list ... that sounds like something that could potentially eat up a lot of tokens if we are doing it by hand. And hence why it should get tooling.' The block now quotes these words exactly (the earlier text quoted only the first half). The test only fails when the requested tool is missing, so it enforces the request.

decisions.summary: The task box goes before the GM-review box (as claims-carry places its boxes). A plan section, if given, goes before the feature's close section, or at the end.
decisions.why: The GM asked for tooling to insert a task 'somewhere in the middle of the task list', not at the end. Putting it before the trailing GM-review and close sections is exactly that middle insertion. The request does not ask to insert at any chosen position, so this narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: Revised from 'about 30 tasks' to a dated count: T41-T64, 24 tasks, each added by a hand-written script of about 1-2k tokens, with two ids (T47, T48) that collided.
decisions.why: A dated, sourced measurement backing the GM's premise that hand insertion costs tokens. It corrects a figure and changes no scope.

decisions.summary: The next id is the highest T<n> across tasks.md and plan.md, plus one, so an id that appears only in a heading is never reused. The script writes the box with its research line, replaces {T} in the SECTION text and puts it before '## T11 - the close', then prints the id.
decisions.why: This is how the requested tool works: choosing the id by hand is what caused the T47/T48 collision. Unchanged since its last CLEAR verdict.

decisions.summary: The archive runs automatically at the end of every successful tick that tick-task.py made, on the tick's feature, and prints the sections it moved.
decisions.why: Amendment 8: 'perhaps that should be something that is run automatically when certain actions are taken ... make our tooling do the thing correctly automatically every time'. The GM left the action open; the tick is the action that finishes a section's last task, so it is the point at which a section first becomes archivable. Printing what moved is the 'says so' the done line measures, not added scope.

decisions.summary: An archive error never refuses the tick (already written); the error is printed.
decisions.why: Refusing after the tick is written cannot make the archive happen and cannot unwrite the tick, so a refusal would not serve 'do the thing correctly automatically every time'; the error is surfaced, not swallowed, and the next tick re-runs the archive. No case is carved out of when the archive runs.

decisions.summary: make plan-archive's rule stays as 375 FR-044 has it (every task of a section ticked, its review CLEAR); the archive never moves an open task's section.
decisions.why: The GM asked for the existing archive to run automatically, not for a different archive rule; preserving the rule is the request as written.

decisions.summary: Tooling only; done is one goal, with a test in test_plan_gate.py or the tick's own test red without it.
decisions.why: The test only fails when the requested automatic archive is absent: enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope (GM 2026-09-20). One goal per task is FR-015.

decisions.summary: A claimed module-level constant counts as changed when its value or its claim line differs between the merge base and the head.
decisions.why: The arbiter's fix fires 'when a claimed constant's value or derivation changes'; the value compare carries the value, the claim line carries the derivation (DIKEPOND_WATER_INSET going from a literal 23 to a derived value changes both).

decisions.summary: Pages are searched for the OLD value as a whole number, whatever unit follows it (changed from a fixed unit list ft/px/%/acres).
decisions.why: The arbiter asks for pages that 'still state the old figure'; no unit list is in the fix, so dropping the list moves the rule toward the arbiter's words, and not matching digits inside longer numbers only stops false matches.

decisions.summary: Only pages that link a question the constant's claim cites are kept (four of the seven pages stating '23 ft').
decisions.why: Implied by the arbiter's own words: the fix flags pages stating the old figure 'for that unit', so some way of tying a page's figure to the constant is required, and without one every page containing that number would be flagged. The plan's measurement (2026-10-18) puts the stale pages that state 23 ft (0022, 0025, plus 0027) inside the four linking pages, so on the case that prompted the fix the filter drops no stale page that states the figure. The purpose, catching stale figures at the edit, is kept. If a stale page stating the figure but not linking the cited question is ever found, this ruling's factual basis is gone.

decisions.summary: 0024, one of the arbiter's named examples, is not reached: it states the split as 'six in ten' and no figure; the claims rounds still read it.
decisions.why: The arbiter's mechanism is figure-based ('flag every research drawing page that still states the old figure'), and 0024 states no figure, so that mechanism cannot reach it. A link rule would not either: measured 2026-10-18, 0024 links no question the claim cites. Of the named examples, 0022 and 0025 state the figure and are caught; 0024 is a different kind of case and the arbiter's sentence does not cover it. The plan says so openly and leaves it to the existing claims rounds, so no case is quietly dropped.

decisions.summary: A flag only, never a refusal, printed by claims-owed from scripts/record/claims.py as 'stale figure: <page> states <figure> (<constant> was <old>)'; a test in test_claims_index.py red without it.
decisions.why: The arbiter says 'the claims check in scripts/record/claims.py should flag'; a flag in that check is what was asked, and a test that fails only when the flag is missing enforces it.

decisions.summary: Tooling-only fix: archiving a finished plan section never makes a review owed; a test red without it; the exit taken is (c), a rule that removes the case.
decisions.why: Amendment 6 asks the overnight run to 'implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way', and amendment 8 asks that the plan archive be run automatically and that the tooling 'do the thing correctly automatically every time'. An archive that turns an already-reviewed block into an owed review is a defect in exactly that automatic tooling; fixing it with a test serves those words and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: block_status's removed-block loop skips a recorded key when plan-done.md holds a block of that key whose text is typo_only against the reviewed text (record's text, else history's at its digest), the same judgment a live block in plan.md already gets; digest match still skips, anything beyond a typo is still owed.
decisions.why: It does not loosen review: it applies to an archived block the same typo rule the live check already applies, so moving a section to plan-done.md changes nothing about whether a review is owed - which is what the archive is meant to guarantee (moving a finished section voids nothing). Changes beyond typo scale remain owed, so no reviewed-text guarantee is given up. No part of the GM's request is narrowed.

decisions.summary: land-tooling.sh runs the lint check first and alone; a lint failure stops at once with its output and the ruff format line, before the guard suites and tooling tests start; a passing lint goes on to the other two in parallel as now.
decisions.why: A tooling performance fix, which amendment 6 asks for in the GM's words ('Please make sure to implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'), made on a defect measured on 2026-10-18 from .git/land-tooling.log (a 0.05 s lint failure reported only after a 122.20 s step). It takes nothing out of anything the GM asked for or anything the spec requires: no FR in spec-index.md governs land-tooling's order of checks (FR-017 to FR-019 are about the push, the arbiter fix command and the ledger). Every check still runs on a landing that passes lint. The Approach's constraint 'every check's failure is still reported' (T52) holds for the checks that run; the suites skipped after a lint failure have no result to report, and the landing fails either way. The constraint is a plan-internal one, not the request's, so this does not narrow anything.

decisions.summary: Done as one goal: a landing whose lint fails stops before the suites start, checked by tests/hooks/test-land-tooling.sh, which is red without the change.
decisions.why: A test whose only job is to enforce D86. Enforcing what was asked is not extra scope (GM 2026-09-20). It is one goal, as FR-015 requires.

decisions.summary: Fix plan_bundle.build, feature 375's plan-review bundler, inside feature 385 as a tooling task, because T65's plan review was handed 385's FR-005 where the block meant 375's requirement.
decisions.why: Amendment 6 (the GM, verbatim): 'Please make sure to implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way.' A bundle that gives the reviewer a different requirement from the one the block cites is a tooling defect found during this feature's own work. This bundle shows the defect too: its spec-cited.md carries 385's FR-005 and none of 375's FR-044/FR-046.

decisions.summary: build reads '(?:feature )?NNN(?:'s|,)? (FR|SC)-NNN' as a citation of feature NNN's requirement and writes it to spec-cited.md under a '<!-- feature NNN -->' line.
decisions.why: This is the mechanism of the fix. It serves the goal that the reviewer reads the requirement the block names. The request does not settle this design detail.

decisions.summary: When there are no specs/NNN-* directories, or more than one, the qualified id is left out, the same way an unknown id is left out today.
decisions.why: With no directory there is nothing to include. With several, which one is meant is undecidable. This repeats the bundler's existing unknown-id behavior and removes nothing the GM asked for.
