decisions.id: D85(c) - bare ids stay the reviewed feature's
decisions.summary: An unqualified id still resolves against the reviewed feature only. A block citing another feature writes that feature beside every id it means, and the tool does not guess.
decisions.why: This is a design choice inside a tooling improvement and narrows no request clause. The Done line covers both cases: the qualified form gets the other feature's paragraph, and the same-numbered local requirement is included only when the block also cites it bare.

decisions.summary: spec-index.md keeps indexing only the reviewed feature's requirements.
decisions.why: The goal is about cited requirements (spec-cited.md). Leaving the index alone keeps the change to what the defect needs.

decisions.summary: One goal: the four qualified forms bundle 375's FR-044 headed with its feature. tests/tooling/test_plan_blocks.py is red without it.
decisions.why: The test exists only to enforce the requested fix (GM 2026-09-20). It is one goal, per FR-015.

decisions.summary: make task-add, when plan.md holds a **Lands open**: line, appends the new task id to it and writes the box with [lands-open]; the line's block still owes its review (make plan-delta).
decisions.why: Amendment 6 asks for obvious tooling/process improvements along the way, amendment 8 asks for task-insertion tooling and that the tooling do the thing correctly automatically every time rather than rely on remembering. The defect is measured (T10's push refused over T66/T67). The guard it touches is kept: the line's edit still owes its block review, so the reviewed-plan condition of the landing rule is not bypassed.

decisions.summary: A plan with no **Lands open**: line is left untouched by task-add.
decisions.why: Leaves existing behavior for features that do not land task by task; narrows nothing the GM asked for, since the request concerns the task-by-task landing that tripped.

decisions.summary: make test-file runs ruff format --force-exclude over the .py files changed against the merge base with origin/main (committed, uncommitted and untracked) before pytest, printing 'test-file: formatted <files>' when any changed and staying silent otherwise.
decisions.why: Amendment 8 (the GM): 'anytime that you can just forget to do ... make our tooling do the thing correctly automatically every time', and 'something that is run automatically when certain actions are taken'; amendment 6 asks for 'any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'. Running the formatter in the step a session already runs before every landing, so a forgotten make format can no longer reach a lint, is that request carried out directly. Printing what it reformatted reports the automatic action; it adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: The gate's and land-tooling's ruff format --check stay check-only (no rewrite at the push).
decisions.why: The request asks for automation where a step can be forgotten; it never asks for the push to rewrite files. Leaving the existing checks as they are keeps behavior the GM did not ask to change, and the checks stay as the backstop for a session that skips test-file. Nothing asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: Only .py files the clone changed against its merge base with origin/main are formatted.
decisions.why: This limits the automatic rewrite to the session's own work. It removes nothing the request covers: the forgotten step being automated is formatting the Python the session changed. Formatting files the session did not touch would be a change nobody asked for.

decisions.summary: New tests/tooling/test_test_file_format.py, red without the format step.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested automation: delete the format step and the test has nothing left to check (GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: A tooling task: a plan-review bundle must carry the decision a block cites from another feature, not this feature's same-numbered decision.
decisions.why: Amendment 6 asks the overnight run to 'implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'; a review bundle that hands the reviewer the wrong D18 (385's sty predicate for 375's) is a defect in the plan-stage review tooling this feature runs on, and fixing it is exactly such an improvement. It adds no behavior beyond reading the cited text.

decisions.summary: D85's qualified-citation reader widened from FR/SC to decisions: (?:plan )?D<n> after a feature number resolves from that feature's plan.md + plan-done.md through the same paragraph reader, under the same <!-- feature NNN --> line; an unknown id is left out.
decisions.why: It extends D85's existing rule to the one id kind it missed, using the same sources this feature's own decisions are read from and the same unknown-id handling D85 already sets; it narrows nothing the request or spec asks for, and its done-test (red without it) only enforces the fix.

decisions.summary: The approved proposal's second escape (a turn ending with a question to the GM) is dropped; a turn that truly waits on the GM sets the feature down with WHY="awaiting the GM on <what>" instead (Approach items 2 and 9, D89).
decisions.why: A departure from the approved proposal (amendment 8, 22:38Z, approved by 'I do like all of your other proposals'), so presumed wrong, but it passes on two grounds. (1) The GM's own words imply it: the check he asked for is 'whether or not the feature is either still in progress or has been correctly set down'. That gives two states and no third. A turn that ends on a question, with nothing running and no set-down, is neither. The question escape was the session's addition, not his. (2) Keeping it would defeat the request's stated purpose, and the failure is concrete: 'stopping with tasks partially done is a constant problem with the Opus line of models', and the classic form of that stop is a summary ending 'Shall I go on to the next task?' while the GM sleeps. The question escape lets exactly that turn through. Nothing the escape served is lost: a real wait on the GM is still allowed, as a recorded set-down with a reason, which is the 'correctly set down' state he named. The departure is stated openly in the plan rather than buried.

decisions.summary: IN PROGRESS = the last task-start's feature has an open box other than the GM-review box, and its status line does not close it.
decisions.why: This is how the GM's 'still in progress' is put into practice. The GM-review box is the GM's own step, not left work the session can do. Unchanged since the block's last CLEAR verdict.

decisions.summary: RUNNING = a background command or async agent in the transcript with no later task notification of its id.
decisions.why: Carries the approved escape 'something is still running that will wake the session'. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: SET-DOWN = a set-downs.jsonl row for the feature at or after the task-start, written by make set-down F= WHY= with a reason of two words or more.
decisions.why: Carries the approved 'make set-down F= WHY= record' and the GM's 'correctly set down'. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Silent in a clone with no task-start. Fails open, recorded, on any read error.
decisions.why: With no task-start, no feature has been begun, and the GM asked for a check 'when a feature is begun'. Failing open guards against a Stop guard that holds a session in a loop. The failure is recorded, so it is not silently allowed. Unchanged since the CLEAR verdict.

decisions.summary: The refusal names the open-task count, the first open task and the make set-down command. Each firing is logged.
decisions.why: The refusal names the next step, as Approach item 9 requires. Its wording is not a fidelity matter.

decisions.summary: ledger_owed.py --write-plan-reviews appends the filled row of every owed pass whose subject starts 'MODE 4: PLAN REVIEW', its where cell 'the plan-verdict record (make plan-verdict)'; land-tooling.sh and sync-with-main.sh done run it before their ledger check and commit dev/review-ledger.md when it wrote any
decisions.why: Amendment 5 item 3 (the session: plan reviews' ledger rows filled by hand, 'could be pre-filled from the recorded plan verdict'), approved by the GM ('file amendment 5 for the 3 tooling fixes'); amendment 8 ('make our tooling do the thing correctly automatically every time') and amendment 6 ('implement any obvious ... tooling ... improvements'). FR-019's rule that the acted-on cell names where the pass was recorded is kept: a plan review is recorded by make plan-verdict. Widens automation; narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: only MODE 4 plan-review passes are written automatically; every other owed pass still refuses as now and keeps FR-019's make ledger-owed WRITE= route
decisions.why: Amendment 5 item 3 names plan reviews only; FR-019 (write each other row from the agent's reply with the session's word on what was acted on) is left whole for other checks. Not a carve-out from anything requested.

decisions.summary: the rows are written and committed at landing (land-tooling, sync-with-main.sh done), before the ledger check, never while a gate runs
decisions.why: FR-019 requires the row before a push; FR-010 refuses a tree write under the session's own gate. Writing at landing satisfies both.

decisions.summary: Goal, constraints, order, exits and Done line (unchanged from the text last judged CLEAR): a block differing from its reviewed text only by ids appended to its Lands open line is not owed; any other change, an id removed among them, is owed.
decisions.why: Byte-identical to the CLEAR text in earlier.md; it carries the round arbiter's fix as the block quotes it (the arbiter stands where the GM was asked, feature 379; request.md itself carries no arbiter ruling, so the authority for this block is the plan's quotation of it) and keeps FR-043's default for every other change.

decisions.summary: A reordering, or an id dropped or repeated, on the Lands open line is owed, with a test showing a reorder-only edit owed.
decisions.why: This is the arbiter's own 'any other change to the block, an id removed among them, is owed as now' and FR-043's default that a changed block owes its review. It removes an over-exemption the earlier subset wording carried (a reorder, or a reorder plus an addition, would have passed as a superset); it brings the rule closer to FR-043, not further from it.

decisions.summary: The Lands open line is read as an ordered list: the block is not owed only where the reviewed ids are the current line's start (ids appended), not where they are merely a subset.
decisions.why: It brings the mechanism into line with the Done line already judged CLEAR ('only by ids appended'). It matches the arbiter's 'a task id added by make task-add' exactly if task-add writes the new id at the end of the line. That premise is not settled by the bundle, and the arbiter's required test ('a test showing such a delta is CLEAR without a dispatch') is what settles it: that test must be driven by make task-add's real output, not a hand-appended id, so that a mid-line insertion by task-add would turn it red. That test enforces the arbiter's fix; it is not new scope.

decisions.summary: The two questions become new numbered items 10 and 11 of checklist.md part A (not sub-bullets under item 4).
decisions.why: Change 7 of the step-back report, approved by the GM's 'I do like all of your other proposals' (amendment 8), asks for 'Two new checklist items in the start-of-task Approach'. Two new numbered part A items is the literal reading, and under D8 a numbered item is one the gate refuses a tick without, which honors the GM's rule 'a checklist item or a tool, never a reminder'. This revision follows the request more closely than the earlier CLEAR version (sub-bullets under item 4).

decisions.summary: Items 1-9 keep their numbers; 10 and 11 are appended.
decisions.why: This is how the items are placed. It narrows nothing the request asked for and keeps answers already written meaning what they meant.

decisions.summary: Item 10: 'Before moving a constant. List every use of it and what each one measures'.
decisions.why: It carries 'list every use of a constant before moving it'. Adding 'what each one measures' serves the incident the proposal came from (T09 did not read what BUNDLE_PITCH measured) and asks no more than listing the uses already implies.

decisions.summary: Item 11: 'Before fitting things into room. Write the capacity arithmetic (how many, how wide, against how much room) before rolling anything'.
decisions.why: It carries 'write the capacity arithmetic before running experiments'. In this project the experiments in question are rolls (T06's 20-minute run), so 'before rolling anything' is the same moment. The parenthesis spells out what capacity arithmetic is.

decisions.summary: Item 10 may be answered 'n/a' when no constant is moved.
decisions.why: Judged on its own. The GM's words carry this condition already: 'list every use of a constant before moving it' only applies when a constant is moved. Asking for the list when none is moved would have no object. The rule exists to stop a constant moving before anyone knows its uses, and an n/a on a task that moves nothing does not weaken that.

decisions.summary: Item 11 may be answered 'n/a' when nothing is being fitted into room.
decisions.why: Judged on its own. Capacity arithmetic can only be written where there is a capacity question, so for a task with none it is impossible, not merely awkward. The trigger 'fitting things into room' covers the motivating case exactly (T06: households x farmstead width against the margin's length), so the rule still reaches what it is for.

decisions.summary: An open task whose Approach predates the change must answer items 10 and 11 before its tick; ticked tasks are not reopened.
decisions.why: The request puts the items in the start-of-task Approach. The existing D8 gate makes any unticked task answer every numbered part A item, so this follows from enforcing what was asked and adds no carve-out. Finished tasks have no start left to ask at.

decisions.summary: tests/tooling/test_approach_gate.py shows an Approach answering items 1-9 alone is refused; red without items 10 and 11.
decisions.why: This is enforcement of the request. Delete the two items and the test has nothing left to check, so it serves the request rather than adding scope.

decisions.summary: make where-time F=<n> [SINCE=<ISO>] prints the step-back's per-task table and agents table, implemented in scripts/measure/where_time.py promoted from the scratch script
decisions.why: This is the step-back report's change 8, verbatim 'make where-time produces the tables above', which the GM approved in amendment 8 ('I do like all of your other proposals'; he declined only change 2). The F= and SINCE= arguments and the script's location are implementation choices inside that target.

decisions.summary: Every gap from a session's Stop to its next UserPromptSubmit is booked as 'between turns', however many events fall inside, never as 'thinking'. Waiting on background work and idle time are not told apart in that column; the agents table and the background-run column say what ran.
decisions.why: The goal is that the tables' idle time is right. Item 4 measures the failure it fixes: about 80 minutes of the overnight stall were split by hook events and booked as thinking. Not telling background waits from idle inside this one column narrows nothing. FR-014's waiting bucket groups a subagent, a background run and the GM under one heading, and the subagents' own work still appears in the agents table. A woken turn fires UserPromptSubmit (measured, item 4), so its work goes to its task and not to between turns.

decisions.summary: Each gap is booked to the task active at the gap's start, in feature_report.split_time's categories, with 'between turns' added
decisions.why: This reuses the existing categories so that where-time agrees with make feature-report (FR-005/FR-014). It adds one category and removes none.

decisions.summary: tests/tooling/test_where_time.py, red without the between-turns booking
decisions.why: Its only job is to enforce the approved target and its idle column. It verifies the request and adds no scope.

decisions.summary: block_status skips a '### T<n> part B (...)' block only when it decides nothing, read from its own answers: item 4 'No', item 5 'Neither', and every D<n> it names defined elsewhere in plan.md or plan-done.md; a part B that changes a rule, tunes a number, moves an earlier placement or names a new D-id is owed a review as now.
decisions.why: Implements the GM-approved change 3 of the step-back report (amendment 8: 'I do like all of your other proposals'): 'A part B is checked mechanically; only one that adds a new decision gets a spec-fidelity review'. The check is mechanical (read from the block's own answers and D-ids), as asked. Changing a rule, tuning a number or moving an earlier placement is a decision whether or not it carries a D-id, so owing those a review is what 'only one that adds a new decision' means, not a carve-out from it; the earlier text (D-ids only) let an unlabeled decision skip, and this version closes that gap without reviewing any part B that decides nothing. Under FR-043 the skip removes a block's review only when it adds no decision.

decisions.summary: A part B's items stay make tick's to check (approach_gate refusal of unanswered items), unchanged.
decisions.why: The 'checked mechanically' half of change 3; it keeps existing behavior the request relies on and adds nothing.

decisions.summary: tests/tooling/test_plan_gate.py red without the rule: a No/Neither part B naming no new D-id is not owed; one answering Changing/Tuning, Yes to item 4, or naming a new D-id is.
decisions.why: A test whose only effect is to enforce the requested rule (GM 2026-09-20: enforcement of what was asked is not unrequested scope).

decisions.summary: The task's warrant is amendment 6 ('implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way') applying CLAUDE.md's house style (American spellings, corrected rather than refused) to two writers the hook does not see; replaces the earlier block's quotation of a session reply that request.md does not carry.
decisions.why: Amendment 6 is in request.md verbatim and is dated 2026-10-18; the fix is measured (a gate red on `grey` copied by claims.py record from a reply) and only extends an existing GM rule to an unseen route, which is an obvious tooling improvement rather than new behavior the GM did not ask for.

decisions.summary: Correct the two writers that copy agent words into tracked files: claims.py record (index notes) and apply_edits.py (EDIT new text).
decisions.why: Serves the stated goal (an agent's British spelling never reaches a tracked file through a tool) and nothing beyond it; no other writer or behavior is added.

decisions.summary: Extract the hook's plain-text correction into hm_house.americanize(text), called by the hook as before and by the two writers; PAIRS stays the one table.
decisions.why: Refactor that keeps one table and the hook's behavior unchanged; settles how, not what.

decisions.summary: claims.py record corrects each note parsed from a reply, not the whole reply, so a claim key or path with a British spelling still matches.
decisions.why: Narrows 'American spellings everywhere' to the prose the tool writes. Literal application is physically impossible here: a key or path rewritten no longer identifies its claim or file, so the record would fail. A key or path names something already in the repository rather than bringing an agent's spelling in, so the goal (no new British spelling enters through the tool) and the gate it protects are untouched.

decisions.summary: apply_edits.py corrects an EDIT's new text only; the old text is matched as written.
decisions.why: The old text is a match anchor and is never written to the file, so the house style has nothing to correct in it.

decisions.summary: An EDIT on specs/*/request.md is not corrected, as the hook does not correct one.
decisions.why: Implied by the GM's own rule cited in constraint 2: the GM's own writing is never corrected.

decisions.summary: A quotation (blockquote, q, corner brackets, curly quotes) is held out of correction as the hook holds it.
decisions.why: The house style rule itself keeps a quotation of another's text.

decisions.summary: test_claims_index.py and test_apply_edits.py red without the correction.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested behavior only; deleting the behavior leaves the tests nothing to check.

decisions.summary: task_current, where the section digest differs, compares earlier and current text with every part B that decides_nothing (D94) removed from both, by the existing typo rule; a part B that decides is left in and still owes the section's review.
decisions.why: Implements the GM's approved change 3 (2026-10-18): 'A part B is checked mechanically; only one that adds a new decision gets a spec-fidelity review.' Today a quiet part B, though itself skipped by D94, stales its task's section verdict and re-owes review of the section's other blocks - a review caused by a part B that adds no decision, which change 3 says should not happen. D99 removes exactly that cost and nothing more: the quiet/deciding test is D94's own, unchanged; a deciding part B stays in the comparison; any other edit to the section still changes the comparison and is owed as now (constraint 2). A part B that flips between quiet and deciding changes the stripped text and is owed, so the exemption cannot launder a decision.

decisions.summary: Only quiet part Bs are taken out of the section comparison; every other change to the section is owed as now; a test in tests/tooling/test_plan_gate.py red without the change.
decisions.why: States the boundary of D99 at the GM's words (only a decision-adding part B is reviewed) and adds a test whose only effect is to enforce that the requested behavior happens - enforcement of the request, not new scope.

decisions.summary: land-tooling.sh appends {task, files, outcome, utc} to <git dir>/land-tooling.jsonl from an exit trap, so a run that dies early still leaves a row whose outcome is the step it stopped at; the task is the clone's active one from task-starts.jsonl
decisions.why: The arbiter's fix needs 'that task's last make land-tooling FILES' and whether 'that landing's log ends in a failure'; a per-run row of files and outcome is the record that makes both checkable. Moving the write into an exit trap only widens it to runs that die early, which are exactly the failed landings the fix is for (the T72 incident). Mechanism, not scope.

decisions.summary: the check fires when the NOTE matches \blanded\b case-insensitively (re.I), so 'Landed via make land-tooling' is caught
decisions.why: The fix scopes the refusal to a NOTE that 'says landed'; 'Landed' at a sentence start says the same thing, so matching in any case enforces the fix's own trigger rather than adding to it. A note that does not say landed is still not checked, as the fix states.

decisions.summary: a failed last outcome refuses naming the log; a landed one refuses where git diff --quiet origin/main -- <file> fails (after a fetch) for any file in its FILES, naming the file
decisions.why: These are the fix's two conditions verbatim ('any file ... still differs from origin/main, or ... that landing's log ends in a failure'), each refusal naming what the fix says to name for that condition (the differing file, the failed log). The fetch makes origin/main current so the comparison is against main as it stands.

decisions.summary: a task with no land-tooling row is not refused (it did not land through the tool, or lands with its feature)
decisions.why: Implied by the fix's own words: the refusal is defined over 'that task's last make land-tooling FILES' and 'that landing's log'; with no land-tooling run there is no FILES list and no log, so the condition has nothing to test. Refusing such ticks would be a new rule the arbiter did not give (and would block tasks that land with their feature through the ordinary push). It does not gut the fix's purpose: the incident it answers was a tick claiming a failed land-tooling run, which always leaves a row under D98-record.

decisions.summary: Pop-ups are grouped by the check agent they owe (modal-form, modal-depiction, modal-research), not by a shared template.
decisions.why: The approved step-back change 1 says 'pop-ups that share a template are checked once as a group'; amendment 1 item 2, also GM-approved, says 'one agent should judge all the pop-ups that cite a changed page, not one agent per pop-up'. Grouping every pop-up that owes the same check covers both readings and is no narrower than either; pop-ups that share a template owe the same check, so they are batched.

decisions.summary: A batch is named only where two or more unanswered pop-ups owe the same check.
decisions.why: A group of one is not a group; a single owed pop-up is already one agent reading one pop-up, which is what the request asks for.

decisions.summary: record_owed.report prints one 'batched: make modal-bundle KIND="<kinds>" FOR=<agent>' line per check and writes the batches to <git dir>/modal-batches.json with the time.
decisions.why: This carries the request: the measured cause (90 single-pop-up dispatches, every one following record-owed's one-KIND line) is fixed at the listing every session follows, on every run - the tool, not a reminder. It reuses T02's multi-KIND bundle (D12) rather than adding a new one.

decisions.summary: A triage-owed pop-up, which goes to make modal-triage first, is left out of the batched line.
decisions.why: Implied by the GM's own amendment 1 item 1 (FR-008): a re-owed pop-up is triaged against what the last check read before any check is spent, and triage may find it owes nothing. Batching it before triage would spend the full check FR-008 exists to save. The block's wording ('goes to make modal-triage first') is sequencing, not exclusion; the ruling rests on that premise - a pop-up still owed after triage is batched on the next record-owed listing like any other. Were triaged pop-ups instead left permanently to single dispatches, it would recreate the measured failure for exactly the pop-ups a page change re-owes and would be NOT LEGITIMATE.

decisions.summary: hm_checks.dispatch refuses a pop-up agent whose MANIFEST names one pop-up when that pop-up is in a current batch of two or more for the same agent, naming the batched command.
decisions.why: The GM's rule is a tool, never a reminder; a refusal whose only reach is the single-pop-up dispatch of a check the request says is checked once as a group enforces the request and nothing else. It covers the measured failure mode (single dispatches); a hand-built partial batch is not reached, which is within because the batched line D100 prints is the route sessions take to a multi-KIND command.

decisions.summary: The guard reads only a modal-batches.json written in the last two hours; no file, or an older one, refuses nothing.
decisions.why: A refusal on a stale snapshot would refuse dispatches outside the request - batches already answered or changed by later page edits - so the rule cannot be applied without a current record. Computing the batch at dispatch would cost record-owed's 4.4 s / 3.3 s (labeled measurement) on every dispatch. The purpose survives: D100 makes the batched line appear on every record-owed run, which is where the 90 single dispatches came from; D101 is the backstop. The two-hour figure is an implementation knob, not a target.

decisions.summary: BATCH_OK="<reason>" in the prompt lets a single dispatch through, recorded like the guard's other escapes.
decisions.why: Every guard in this project carries a recorded-reason escape; the request does not ask for an unescapable guard, and a recorded escape is a logged, auditable act rather than a silent departure. It also recovers from a false refusal where a batch member has since been answered.

decisions.summary: Owed-ness is computed in record-owed and read from a file at dispatch, not recomputed by the hook.
decisions.why: Design choice inside the request, backed by the labeled 2026-10-19 timing; it changes no scope.

decisions.summary: Done names one goal; tests/tooling/test_record_owed.py and tests/hooks/test-pair-hooks.sh are red without it; budget 60 min; order record_owed, then hm_checks, then tests.
decisions.why: The tests only fail when the requested batching or its refusal is absent - enforcement of the request (GM 2026-09-20), and one goal per task is amendment 4's own checklist item.

decisions.summary: task_current compares a task's section and its reviewed text with ARCHIVE_LINE taken out of both (as block_digest already does per block); digest match and typo rule otherwise unchanged
decisions.why: Feature 375 FR-044 says the archive's generated line owes no review; the per-task section comparison not stripping it made T79's reviewed blocks owed again after an auto-archive (amendment 8's 'run automatically' request). Stripping exactly that generated line from both texts carries out FR-044 for the section check, and nothing more: no other kind of edit stops counting, and no review is waived for authored text. Amendment 6 also approves fixing obvious tooling defects along the way.

decisions.summary: A module-level dict-literal constant carrying its own claims is read as a section: one block per entry, each claim fingerprinted by its own line ('section-claim'), core stays the whole value's.
decisions.why: This is the step-back's change 4, 'Per-entry keying of a dictionary's claims', which the GM ordered worked as a task (amendment 8: 'instead of filing me per entry key ring feature, you should just work it. As a task on this existing feature'). It applies 375 FR-002's line-scoped rule to a dict, so an entry added re-opens only the claims it bears on, which is the purpose. Limiting it to module-level dict literals does not narrow the request: claims attach to claims-index units, the measured population of claimed dicts is 57 module-level dict constants (labeled with its date and method), and the motivating case, _OVERLAP_EXEMPT, is one of them.

decisions.summary: claims.py owed owes 'section triage' for any unit with blocks whose recorded core differs (sections and dicts alike); a claim line edited still owes that claim in full; backfill-sections re-keys a dict claim only when its row is current under the old whole-value fingerprint, records its core and block digests, leaves an owed row owed, and runs once.
decisions.why: This is how the per-entry keying gets carried out. The triage still reads every changed entry against every claim and sends the touched ones to impl-drift, so nothing the old fingerprint caught goes unchecked. It only stops an unrelated entry from re-owing every claim, which is the cost the step-back measured on _OVERLAP_EXEMPT. The backfill clears nothing that is owed: a row current under the stricter whole-value fingerprint is current under the line fingerprint too, and an owed row stays owed. That keeps the rule from settling claims that nobody reviewed.

decisions.summary: Done is one goal, measured: an entry added owes a triage rather than 'code changed', a claim line edit owes in full, the backfill adds no owed dict claim it did not owe before, and two test files go red without it.
decisions.why: These tests only fail when the requested keying is missing, so they enforce what the GM asked for and are not added scope (GM 2026-09-20). One goal per task follows amendment 4.

decisions.summary: Each between-turns window, from a Stop to the session's next UserPromptSubmit, is booked whole to one class chosen by the prompt that ends it: gm false (a notification) is waiting on work; gm true is the GM, or the GM away when the window passed an hour.
decisions.why: Proposal G, which the GM's 'build all 7 of those as 385 tasks' approves, is 'a between-turns window classed by what ended it' and 'fold the scratch split in'. Classing by the ending prompt is G's own wording. The one-hour line between the GM and the GM away is the scratch split's (Approach item 4 measured it with wt2.py, 103 vs 357 minutes), and G's stated cost, 'where-time cannot tell waiting from idle', needs exactly that line. Nothing the GM asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: make where-time replaces the single 'between turns' column with three columns (waiting on work / the GM / the GM away) that add up to the old column, and tests/tooling/test_where_time.py is red without the split.
decisions.why: The three columns ARE G's split, and because they add up to T77's column nothing it reported is lost. The test only fails when the requested split is missing, so it enforces the request rather than adding scope (GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: plan_gate.record and record_blocks pass every free-text string field of a decision (why, summary and the like) through hm_house.americanize; id, class, ruling and the digests are written as given
decisions.why: Proposal E, approved in amendment 9 ('build all 7 of those'), is 'make plan-verdict passes the reviewer's text through americanize'. Both record paths are make plan-verdict (the TASK=/whole-plan route and the BLOCKS=1 route), so covering both is what the proposal says, not a widening. Leaving id, class, ruling and the digests alone is not a carve-out from 'the reviewer's text': they are keys, enumerated values and hashes the gate matches on, not prose, and changing them would break the record the proposal is meant to keep green.

decisions.summary: text inside a quotation is held out of the correction, as the house-style hook holds it out
decisions.why: The GM's words fix the method: 'as T78 does for notes', i.e. the existing americanize with its existing behavior, which this block says holds quotations out the way the hook does. The purpose is that a reviewer's spelling never turns the gate red; a word the hook does not flag cannot turn it red, so holding out what the hook holds out leaves that purpose intact while keeping verbatim quotations verbatim. The measured incident in item 4 is a word the preflight DID flag, so it falls inside what the correction reaches, and item 9's done-test asserts exactly that case.

decisions.summary: the call is added in plan_gate.record and the block record, then a test in tests/tooling/test_plan_gate.py red without it
decisions.why: The test only fails when the requested correction is absent: it enforces proposal E rather than adding scope.

decisions.summary: preflight.tree's tree-move check leaves out only the outputs of the maps the gate's own run log reports as 'ROLLED this run'; any other changed file, including another map's pool output, is still a tree move
decisions.why: It narrows 375 FR-004 (refuse green when any tracked file changed during the gate), but the GM's amendment 9 approves exactly this carve-out: proposal D, 'the gate commits (or ignores) the manifests it re-rolled itself instead of calling them a tree move'. Keying on the maps the gate itself rolled matches 'it re-rolled itself' word for word, and keeps FR-004's purpose (catch a write by anyone else) for every other file, other maps' pool outputs included. The earlier CLEAR text excused every pool map output whoever wrote it; this revision is closer to the request, not further from it.

decisions.summary: the excused files are all of a rolled map's outputs beside its .gen.py (json, png, svg, html, webp), not the json manifest alone
decisions.why: Proposal D says 'manifests'. But its stated purpose is that the gate stops failing on its own re-roll ('a gate per stale manifest'; T87 goal: 'a gate never fails for a pool map it re-rolled itself'). A re-roll rewrites all of that map's tracked outputs, so excusing only the json would still fail the gate on the png/svg/html/webp from the same roll. Taken literally the rule would defeat the request's own purpose. The set is still limited to the rolled map's own outputs, so nothing outside the gate's own write is excused.

decisions.summary: of 'commits (or ignores)' the plan takes 'ignores': the files are left out of the comparison and printed as 're-rolled by the gate - commit them'
decisions.why: The GM's approved proposal offers the two alternatives; picking one, and telling the session to commit what was left out, is inside it.

decisions.summary: tests/tooling/test_preflight.py red without it: a rolled map's outputs are not refused, a move of any other file (another map's pool output too) still refuses
decisions.why: A check that only fails when the requested behavior is missing, and that keeps 375 FR-004 for everything else. It enforces proposal D and is not new scope.

decisions.summary: A quotation is each double-quoted span following the literal 'the GM' (any case, with or without the possessive) within the same sentence of the task's section.
decisions.why: Proposal A (amendment 9, the seven the GM said to build) names its trigger as a section quoting "the GM", putting the literal string in quotes; anchoring the check on that string and the double-quoted span after it is the proposal's own wording put into operation, not a carve-out. Widening from the earlier 'The GM' / 'the GM's' to any case and either form broadens the check toward the proposal.

decisions.summary: A span passes when its words, lowercased with punctuation removed, appear as a contiguous run in request.md folded the same way.
decisions.why: Proposal A refuses 'words not in request.md'. Folding case and punctuation (which come from dictation and typography, not from the GM's words) keeps the test about words; requiring the run rather than scattered single words is the only reading under which the check can catch a misquote like T64's, so it is no narrower than the proposal.

decisions.summary: Every quoted span is checked whatever its length (the earlier four-word floor is gone).
decisions.why: Proposal A sets no length floor; the earlier block's 'a shorter span is a phrase, not a quotation, and is not checked' was the narrowing, and removing it brings the check back to the proposal as written.

decisions.summary: No override: a wrong refusal is cleared by rewording the span or adding the GM's words to request.md verbatim.
decisions.why: Proposal A carries no escape; the earlier QUOTE_OK escape was an addition the proposal did not ask for, and dropping it matches the request. The two ways to clear a refusal are what the refusal message itself names.

decisions.summary: make decide refuses, naming each failing span, with 'add the GM's words to request.md verbatim, or correct the quote'.
decisions.why: Proposal A: '`make decide` refuses ... naming the words'. Placed in make decide (plan_bundle.task_prompt's caller), as the proposal names it.

decisions.summary: tests/tooling/test_plan_blocks.py red without the check; a section whose quotes are all present builds its bundle as now.
decisions.why: A test that fails only when the requested refusal is absent enforces proposal A (GM 2026-09-20: enforcing what was asked is not unrequested scope); the passing case only confirms the check does not change bundles it should leave alone.

decisions.summary: The check works one sentence at a time: each sentence of Approach item 4 that holds a figure must carry its own label, and one label covers only the figures in its own sentence (this replaces the earlier text, where one label anywhere in item 4 covered the whole item).
decisions.why: Proposal C, which the GM approved verbatim ('build all 7 of those', amendment 9), asks for a refusal when a figure has no measured date and method 'beside it'. A label in the figure's own sentence is a closer reading of 'beside it' than a label anywhere in the item. The change moves toward the request and refuses more, not less.

decisions.summary: Dates, clock times and ids (T10, D84, FR-005, a question's 0018) are not counted as figures.
decisions.why: The GM's rule is about measured figures. The label he names, 'measured <date>', itself contains a date, so his own words already treat dates as not being figures. Ids and clock times name things or moments, not quantities.

decisions.summary: Code spans that hold a path, key or command (marked by '/', '::', '=' or 'make ') are set aside. A code span holding a measured value (for example 4.4 s) is read like prose. This narrows the earlier text, which set aside every code span.
decisions.why: Each trigger judged separately. '/', '::' and 'make ' mark paths, dictionary keys and commands. None of them is a measured quantity, so setting them aside narrows nothing the GM asked for. '=' marks an argument or assignment such as F=385. Counting its number as a figure would refuse a plan that holds no unreviewable figure, and nothing could fix that, because a feature number cannot be labeled as measured. That false refusal would cost the review round proposal C exists to save ('a round each time'). The residue: a measured value written as key=value inside a code span would slip past the check. This is an edge of the detector, not a carve-out of the rule. The block's own rule still reads every measured value written as a value, which is how the triggering incident stated its figure ('4.4 s (measured)'). The plan review is the backstop for the rest. Compared with the earlier CLEAR text, this decision makes the check reach further.

decisions.summary: A figure with an m:<key> pointer into measurements.json passes, as an alternative to 'measured YYYY-MM-DD' followed by a method in parentheses.
decisions.why: Taken literally, the GM's words ask for 'measured <date>' and a method beside the figure, and a key is neither. But the request's purpose, which the block states, is that no figure reaches review in a form the review cannot check. An m:<key> entry carries its command, the method in its strongest form, and is the form the review re-runs (make figures). Refusing it would refuse the one label that can be checked mechanically, which defeats the purpose. Accepting it carries out the GM's 'method beside it' by pointer.

decisions.summary: The date label must match measured 20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d and be followed by a method in parentheses.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 'measured <date>' and 'method', made concrete.

decisions.summary: Only Approach item 4 is read. The budget (item 8) and the other items are not checked.
decisions.why: Proposal C names 'an Approach item 4 figure'. Item 8 is a budget, not a measurement.

decisions.summary: make decide refuses and names the first figure without a label. No escape.
decisions.why: This is the refusal proposal C asks for. Having no escape means nothing is excepted.

decisions.summary: Item 5 builds the check next to proposal A's in make decide, then its test. Item 9 makes tests/tooling/test_plan_blocks.py fail without the check.
decisions.why: Order and placement are inside the task. The test only enforces the requested refusal: take the refusal out and the test has nothing left to check.

decisions.summary: Every running spec-fidelity plan review holds what its bundle names: a task preflight's section, a plan-delta review's blocks.
decisions.why: Proposal B (amendment 9) refuses 'an edit to a section whose review is running'. A block under a plan-delta review is the unit that review digests, so it is a section under review. Only spec-fidelity records plan verdicts (AS=spec-fidelity), so its digest is the one that goes stale (the incident in Approach item 4). Limiting the hold to spec-fidelity therefore drops no review the request covers.

decisions.summary: The refusal names the running review's agent and its task or blocks.
decisions.why: The GM's proposal says 'naming the agent'. Naming the task or blocks as well adds no behavior; it only identifies the hold.

decisions.summary: An Edit whose old_string lies in held text, or whose new_string lands in it, is refused. So is a Write whose new content differs from the plan in held text.
decisions.why: These are the plan-write path the proposal names, and the test fires exactly when held text would change. Edits elsewhere pass, as 'an edit to a section whose review is running' implies.

decisions.summary: A Bash write is refused when its write targets include the plan and its command text contains the held heading or any held line. A shell edit that names neither (for example by line number) is not caught.
decisions.why: This leaves a gap in what the request covers: some Bash writes to held text pass. Before a shell command runs, a hook cannot decide in general what text it will change, so an exact test is impossible here. The only exact alternative is refusing every Bash write of the plan while any review runs, which would refuse edits to other sections that the GM's words leave allowed. The text test is the same one the Edit path applies. The gap does not defeat the purpose ('a plan review is never wasted'): plan-verdict's digest check still refuses a stale review, so an edit that slips through costs a round but is never recorded as a wrong verdict.

decisions.summary: PLAN_EDIT_OK="<reason>" passes, and is recorded, only for a hold a dead dispatch left (no agent of that review still running, by the pair state).
decisions.why: The GM's rule covers a section 'whose review is running'. A hold left by a dead dispatch is a review that is not running, so the request already implies letting that edit through. Recording the reason adds no reach.

decisions.summary: A live review's held text has no escape; the session waits for the review to return. The earlier text allowed PLAN_EDIT_OK for any deliberate edit.
decisions.why: This brings the refusal closer to the request, which gives an edit under a running review no escape. Dropping the 'deliberate edit' escape removes a carve-out the GM never asked for, so nothing he asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The suite shows the refusal red without the hook and never green by the escape, and covers a held line as well as the heading.
decisions.why: This enforces the requested refusal and nothing else; with the refusal removed it would have nothing to check.

decisions.summary: Proposal F's per-task attribution is made where it is read: where-time books each gap to the task its tool call names, falling back to the mark; no workflow command moves the mark (item 2, D110)
decisions.why: Proposal F (amendment 9) names its own purpose: 'where-time misbooks tasks' -> 'true per-task numbers'. Followed literally, the mark move defeats that purpose, and the block shows how: deciding T76 while building T75 moves the mark to T76, so T75's later work is booked to T76. The misbooking follows from the mechanism itself and is not an unmeasured premise. The new route reaches the stated purpose: item 4 measured it on 2026-10-19 by the wt3.py join (T10 drops from 320 min to its own work; the evening's tasks come to 5-20 min each). This is the same text that was judged CLEAR before (earlier.md) and it is unchanged.

decisions.summary: Nothing is retired: proposal 6's refusal (a check refused for a task other than the active one), which F says it replaces, was never built (measured 2026-10-19 by a grep of scripts/hooks/)
decisions.why: F says it replaces proposal 6, so not building proposal 6 follows from F's own words, and with nothing built there is nothing to remove. The premise is a measurement that states its method. Its reach is scripts/hooks/ only; a dispatch guard kept anywhere else would not be seen by that grep.

decisions.summary: make decide F= T= and make tick F= T= are booked to the task their T= names
decisions.why: This is F's 'the task they name', applied at read time through the route ruled above.

decisions.summary: make land-tooling FILES= names no task, so its gap goes to the last named task
decisions.why: F moves the mark to 'the task they name'. land-tooling's input names no task, so under F's own words there is no task to move to, and booking to the last named task leaves the attribution where it already was.

decisions.summary: make task-add's new id appears only in its output, so its gap, and any gap after it with no naming call, goes to the last named task rather than to the new task
decisions.why: Judged separately from the other three commands, because F, read literally, would move the mark to the task task-add creates. The concrete failure that justifies the route applies here too. A task is usually added while another task is being worked (FR-015: a second goal found in a task becomes its own task). Moving the mark to the new task would book the rest of the current task's work to a task nobody has started. The new task gets its time as soon as a call names it (its decide or tick T=, its heading, its commit). That serves 'true per-task numbers' better than the literal mark move.

decisions.summary: where_time.tables joins the session transcript (located by the event log's sid) to the events by tool-use id, books a gap to the task its input names when it names exactly one, otherwise to the last named task, otherwise to the mark; a footer gives the minutes booked by each rule
decisions.why: This is the mechanism for the route ruled above. The footer reports which rule booked each minute, which only verifies that the per-task numbers F asks for are true, and adds no new behavior.

decisions.summary: The join, then tests/tooling/test_where_time.py red without it; budget 40 min; exits (c); items 10-11 n/a
decisions.why: The test only enforces the requested attribution. Order and budget decide nothing about scope.

decisions.summary: land-tooling.sh runs its existing ruff check / ruff format --check on the .py files it was given as its first check, after the fetch (so main's lint config is main's) and before the merge and the worktree, dying with ruff's first lines and the ruff format command; every caller goes through it.
decisions.why: The arbiter's fix (hour:385-approach-checklist@27, standing where the GM was asked) asks for 'the same ruff check and format check the landing applies' run so a failure shows 'in seconds'. Moving the lint after the fetch costs about a second and makes the check use the config the landing actually applies, which serves the 'same check' clause rather than narrowing anything; the foreground refusal is carried by the make-only guard, unchanged from the block's last CLEAR text. The landing's own lint (T52, T55, T67) stays.

decisions.summary: The make-only guard runs the same lint on the files named by make land-tooling FILES= or make arbiter-fix-done ... LAND= and refuses the command before it runs.
decisions.why: This is the arbiter's 'refuse before it goes to the background'. arbiter-fix-done LAND= lands tooling through land-tooling (FR-018), so covering it is the same landing, not a new reach.

decisions.summary: A landing naming no .py file is not refused.
decisions.why: The fix lints the Python files the landing carries; with none there is nothing to check.

decisions.summary: Where ruff is not installed, the early lint refuses nothing.
decisions.why: The fix is to run ruff early; with ruff absent the early check can't run at all, so this case is physically impossible rather than a carve-out of convenience. The landing's own lint (T52) stays as it was, so the case loses no check it had before.

decisions.summary: Row 843 (MISLABELED) is taken as T31: MISLABELED is the first kind not yet tried in T05-T10, and row 827, the first such row, is now IN-STEP.
decisions.why: FR-020 asks for a row of a kind not yet tried where one is left, chosen at the task's start. That is how this row was chosen, and it carries out amendment 7's ten more claims.

decisions.summary: Row 841 (the street's joining leg, which reads the same constant) becomes its own task, T32, and is not folded into T31.
decisions.why: FR-015 says a second goal becomes its own task before work on it starts. Row 841 is still a ranking row worked under FR-020, so nothing is dropped.

decisions.summary: Keep FOOTPATH_FABRIC_GAP at 4 ft. 0246's drawing page records a footpath's middle 4 ft off a garden fence as its own map drawing convention, beside the lane's 7 ft, with the reason (measured 2026-10-19, make cohort at 7.0: seeds 3, 4, 903 and 904 newly fail). The claim points at that page, the comment above the constant records it, and no value changes.
decisions.why: Both numbers are O. 0246 calls its 7 ft 'a map drawing convention, not a measured figure', and the 4 ft is feature 328's. The GM's request says an unresearched number is a knob to refine, and the approved checklist's guardrail asks that loosening a rule record its reason where the code changes. D113 records that reason on the page and at the constant. Row 843's own fix offers this route ('0246 must record the 4 ft ... or the code is DRIFTED'). No GM ruling or Research: claim is loosened, so this is not an exception to anything the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Exit (d) is not chosen: seeds are not re-seated to give 17 ft of footpath room.
decisions.why: Re-seating farmhouses so a footpath can keep a margin would move houses for a path. The GM's request rejects exactly that ('Nobody in real life moves their house so that a footpath will join...'). Turning this exit down follows the request; it does not narrow it.

decisions.summary: Order: record first, then the two claims, then the stale comment. Done means the claims check finds it IN-STEP. Budget 60 min.
decisions.why: This is how the work is carried out, and it is the checklist's FR-003 Approach content. It settles nothing the request or spec left open in a narrower way.

decisions.summary: claims.py triaged reads --reply through apply_edits.reply_of (a .jsonl/.output transcript's last assistant reply, else the file as text), as make modal-triaged already does
decisions.why: A tooling defect measured while working T31 (amendment 7's claims): a transcript's reply was read raw and its 18 TOUCHES lines cleared unread. Amendment 6 asks the session to 'implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'; reusing the existing reader narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: a reply with no readable text is refused, naming the file, and clears nothing
decisions.why: The refusal reaches only the defect's own case (an unread reply that would otherwise clear every claim); it guards the claim triage the feature already carries, not another command or agent, and widens no scope beyond the fix amendment 6 authorizes.

decisions.summary: a readable reply with no TOUCHES line clears the bundle as now
decisions.why: Preserves the existing triage rule unchanged rather than excepting any case from what was asked; the GM asked nothing about this rule, so keeping it is not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: done measured by make claims-triaged on a transcript recording its TOUCHES lines, and a test in tests/tooling/test_claims_scoping.py red without the fix
decisions.why: A test whose only effect is to keep the fix in place: enforcement of the requested improvement, not new scope.

decisions.summary: Row 841 is chosen for T32, described as 'the same kind as T31's' (MISLABELED), because T31's claims round found it to be a real drift.
decisions.why: FR-020 says each row is 'a row of a kind not yet tried where one is left', and the proposal the GM approved gives the reason: 'about five ranking rows of different kinds, so the checklist is tested on more than lanes'. The block never says that no untried kind is left among the open rows. Its only reason is that T31 found this row, which is convenience: it is not impossible to pick another kind, the GM's words do not imply it (amendment 7 asks only for '10 more claims'), and taking a second MISLABELED row in a row works against the variety the rule exists for. To fix it, either state, measured with a date and method (a count of the open rows by kind), that no untried kind is left, which puts the pick within FR-020, or choose a row of a kind not yet tried.

decisions.summary: join_to's two _route calls take gap=WEB_FABRIC_GAP (the lane's 7 ft) and its claim cites 0246's 7 ft; no constant's value moves.
decisions.why: This is row 841's own fix ('the joining leg's berth at 0246's 7 ft off a garden fence'), applied to the leg the block measured as drawn at STREET_WIDTH, a lane.

decisions.summary: Order (gap, claim, cohort), one exit (a), a 30 min budget, one measured done-goal.
decisions.why: The checklist answered as FR-003/FR-015 require. One exit is enough because no rule is being fought here: the leg read the wrong constant.

decisions.summary: record_owed.modal_batches and command read modal_triage.touched(store): a pop-up owed only by a moved page that the triage marked touched is treated as an ordinary owed pop-up, so it joins its check's batch and names make modal-bundle. A pop-up not yet triaged keeps make modal-triage and stays out of the batch.
decisions.why: This widens batching rather than narrowing it. It carries out D100's own wording: the triage-owed pop-up goes to make modal-triage FIRST, then joins a batch. That is the condition T81's plan review set for the exclusion. It serves the GM's approved Amendment 1 item 2 ('one agent should judge all the pop-ups that cite a changed page, not one agent per pop-up') and Amendment 8 change 1 (pop-ups checked once as a group). An untriaged pop-up keeps going to triage first, as FR-008 requires, and D100's two-or-more threshold is untouched. Nothing the GM asked for is excepted.

decisions.summary: claims.py record reads --reply through claims_triage.triage_reply (T92's reader) before unelide, so a transcript's last reply is recorded whatever file carries it; a reply with no text is refused, naming the file, and nothing is written.

Amendment 6 asks the session to 'implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'. Reusing T92's reader extends a rule already settled for claims-triaged to its twin command. The refusal on an empty reply only stops an unread reply being recorded as read; it adds no behavior beyond the tool doing what it already claims. Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Order: reader, then empty-reply refusal, then a test in tests/tooling/test_claims_index.py that is red without the fix; one goal (FR-015).
decisions.why: The test only enforces the fix (feature 385's practice and SC-004/SC-009 style), and the single goal follows FR-015. Nothing is excluded.

decisions.summary: Exit (c), add a rule that removes the case (one reader for both commands); budget 15 min.
decisions.why: A choice of mechanism and a time budget inside the task. The checklist names this exit, and no requirement or ruling is relaxed.

decisions.summary: join_to's two _route calls take gap=WEB_FABRIC_GAP (the lane's 7 ft, 0246) instead of FOOTPATH_FABRIC_GAP (4 ft); the leg's claim cites 0246's 7 ft and states the leg is drawn at the street's width, a lane.

Nothing is relaxed or excepted; it is the conform exit, the ranking row's own stated fix, taken as a defect fixed where found under the ranking work FR-020 carries (amendment 7, 'pull in 10 more claims'). No constant's value moves.

decisions.summary: FOOTPATH_FABRIC_GAP becomes 0246's 7 ft.
decisions.why: This is the claim being fixed (FR-020's ranking rows): the code is brought to the attested figure rather than the recorded 4 ft. Nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The door's numbers stop reading the fence gap: new DOOR_STEP_FT (8 ft, front_door's offset) and DOOR_FIXTURE_CLEAR_FT (5 ft, door_off_fixtures' clearance off the farm's own fixtures and grove bands), both held at their pre-change values and labeled UNRESEARCHED, in serve.py, web.py and row_rules.py.

On it, 0246's rule (a lane's middle 7 ft off a garden fence, a household's own way allowed beside its own fence) never governed the door's clearance from its own dooryard: the FOOTPATH_FABRIC_GAP + 1 coupling was ours, which is exactly the GM's 'an arbitrary figure ... we could just change that'. The fence gap itself is applied at 7 ft wherever it reads, the two knobs carry their UNRESEARCHED labels (the request's guardrail: a loosening's reason recorded where the code changes), and the cause was measured before the route was chosen. It would be a narrowing, and a purpose-fatal one, only if door_off_fixtures also kept the door off neighbors' fences, so that a path started inside others' 7 ft band; the block says own ground only.

decisions.why: Completes the claim fix: the record is brought into step with the code and the research.

decisions.summary: T43's item 3 (span_walkable and a household's own garden) stays T43's, where the earlier CLEAR text decided it with T96.
decisions.why: Work moved between tasks, not dropped: T43 still owns it, and FR-015's one goal a task favours it. The ruling's 'worked with it' named the tread-to-wall figure (T43 item 1), which exit (a) still carries.

decisions.id: D119 (room off a grove counted once)

Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed; the block is unchanged since its last CLEAR.

decisions.summary: The flood fill's cell moves from 7 to 2.9 ft so a 32 ft gap between dispersed farms' bands holds a way out at a 12.5 ft band gap (2 x 12.5 + 2.41 x 2.9 = 31.99 <= 32); item 10 now lists every use of the constant (track.py:940 start offset 15.6 ft vs the 16 ft half-gap, track.py:941 fill cost about 5.8x cells only where no sweep bearing is clear, serve.py:420 docstring, the raster test) - arithmetic re-derived here and it holds
decisions.why: An unresearched grid resolution derived from its own stated rule, moved to fit the room the research gives rather than shrinking that room - the refine-an-arbitrary-number exit the GM's request names. Listing every use before moving it is the checklist item the GM approved in Amendment 8 (proposal 7). The change corrects item 10's earlier 'no constant moves', which contradicted D119; it narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: A tooling fix found while working T98 is filed as its own task: a gate re-run after a red preflight is let through by the measure guard.
decisions.why: Amendment 6 (GM, verbatim): 'Please make sure to implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'; amendment 4's one-goal-per-task rule (FR-015) is why it is its own task rather than folded into T98. The fix makes the guard keep its own stated rule ('a run after a red goes through') in a case it was measured to miss on 2026-10-19; it adds no behavior beyond that rule.

decisions.summary: done's preflight failure branch touches <git dir>/gate-preflight-red; measure-hooks.sh lets the full measurement through, without refusing once, when that file is newer than the last green run-log record.
decisions.why: Mechanism for the guard's existing rule; it widens what the guard admits only to the case the rule already names (a red gate, here red at preflight). A tool rather than a reminder, as amendment 1 item 3 and amendment 8 ('make our tooling do the thing correctly automatically every time') ask. Narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.id: Exit (c): an untracked mark rather than a run-log record
decisions.summary: The red preflight is recorded as a mark in the git directory; writing a dev/run-log record is refused because those are tracked files the landing sweeps.
decisions.why: Implementation choice between two routes to the same goal; the request settles neither, and neither route drops any part of the goal.

decisions.id: Item 9: an older preflight failure changes nothing
decisions.summary: A preflight red older than the last green gate does not lift the guard's refusal.
decisions.why: Not an exception to the request: the guard's rule lets through a run after a red, and a red that a later green superseded is not the last result. This keeps the guard's existing refusal for the case its rule already covers, and the GM asked for nothing in that case to change.

decisions.id: Item 9: the test in tests/hooks/test-measure-hooks.sh, red without the fix
decisions.summary: A hook-suite test that fails without the mark.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested behavior only (a tool, never a reminder); it checks nothing beyond D120.

decisions.summary: In hm_planhold.refusal a hold still pending past PENDING_S (its dispatch refused or lost, never launched) is skipped with no PLAN_EDIT_OK escape needed; a launched hold keeps T85's rule.
decisions.why: It narrows D106, which refuses a dead dispatch's hold until PLAN_EDIT_OK is given. The request (amendment 9, proposal B) asks only that 'the plan-write path refuses an edit to a section whose review is running'. A dispatch that never launched has no review running and nothing reading the text, so the exception is implied by the GM's own words. Refusing there is a guard firing on correct work, which the purpose of the proposal (to prevent stale digests from edits under a live review) does not need. A live or launched review's hold is untouched, so the purpose survives.

decisions.summary: A review agent stopped with TaskStop releases its hold as a return does; the PostToolUse hook that pairs dispatch and agent also hears TaskStop.
decisions.why: Against D106 this removes the escape-only path for a hold a stopped (dead) dispatch left. Proposal B's scope is a section 'whose review is running', and a stopped review is not running and reads nothing, so the exception follows from the request's words. The measurement given (two stopped T104 reviews holding for half an hour) is the guard refusing correct work.

decisions.summary: No hold is dropped by another: a running review's hold stands until it returns, is stopped or dies, whatever later dispatch of the same task is refused. This replaces the earlier text's 'hold drops any earlier hold of the same task'.
decisions.why: It keeps D106 and proposal B at full reach: no running review's held text loses its protection because a later dispatch was refused. Dropping the earlier replacement rule removes a path by which a live review's hold could lapse, so this change widens nothing and narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: Order (refusal change, TaskStop release, then tests); exit (c) chosen and 'conform with the escape each time' refused; done names one goal, with tests in tests/tooling/test_plan_edit_refusal.py and test_hm_checks.py red without it.
decisions.why: One goal per task (amendment 4). The tests only enforce the hold rule the request and D106 already ask for. Refusing the escape-each-time exit follows the GM's rule that a guard firing on correct work teaches bypass.

decisions.summary: The mislabeled claim found by T96's impl-drift round is worked as its own task (T100) rather than inside T96.
decisions.why: Amendment 4 (the GM approved 'a second goal becomes its own task', FR-015) and amendment 3 option 3 (a claims finding becomes an open task the feature must fix before it closes). Nothing the GM asked for is dropped; the finding is fixed in this feature.

decisions.summary: Exit (e) conform: the code is left as it is and only the claim's citation changes; done is the claims check finding the claim IN-STEP.
decisions.why: The finding is MISLABELED (the claim says UNRESEARCHED where 0035's drawing page answers it), and the request's claim work (amendments 7 and 9, feature 316's cite-the-page rule) is to make a claim match its research. Changing only the citation, with the claims check as the measured done, is the narrowest fix that does what was asked. If the code did not in fact keep 0035's rule, the claims check fails and the stated goal is not met, so the decision cannot quietly pass a wrong claim. Whether the code keeps 0035's rule is the claims check's call, not a fidelity finding.

decisions.summary: stage_web's claim is reworded to cite 0035's drawing page: a way keeps to its own bank; cuts and joins clipped at watercourses and drawn channels; a join crosses the brook only at a ford, one of the crossing places.
decisions.why: It carries out T100's goal (cite the page that sets the rule, feature 316) and adds no behavior or scope. The wording's accuracy against 0035 (for example, its 'unless crossing saves more than about 150 ft' clause) is for the claims check and the research ladder to judge, not for this review.

decisions.summary: claims.research_why returns 'research changed' when the claim now cites a page absent from its row's recorded pages, ahead of the triage test; feature 318's triage rule stands for every other moved page
decisions.why: A tooling fix found while working a claim task, which amendment 6 authorizes ('implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way'). It narrows nothing that was asked. Feature 318 FR-016 scopes the re-check owed 'after a page edit' to the blocks a claim rested on. A claim relabeled to a page it was never checked against rested on no block of that page, so FR-016's triage cannot reach it, and the measured result (the triage bundle named no claim, and claims-bundle refused it) shows the claim was owed nothing at all. D123 makes such a claim owed a full check and leaves FR-016 as written for every case it covers. That is consistent with this feature's FR-008: a re-check reads against what the last check read.

decisions.summary: exit (c), treat an unread page as changed research; conform (bundling claims by name each time) refused because it relies on remembering
decisions.why: This is the same decision as D123, seen as the checklist exit. Refusing a remembered workaround in favour of tooling follows the GM's amendment 8 ('make our tooling do the thing correctly automatically every time').

decisions.summary: research_why change first, then the test; 20 min; one goal with tests/tooling/test_claims_scoping.py red without it
decisions.why: Execution choices under FR-003 and FR-015 (one goal per task). Done names one goal and a test that enforces it, which is enforcement of the change rather than added scope.

decisions.summary: Take exit (e) conform: the check is brought to 0031's drawing-page rule as written, rather than refining, excepting or re-scoping it.
decisions.why: Amendment 7 asks for ten more claims taken and the original request asks that rules be tested against the research; conforming a check to a research page (O) it currently contradicts is the plain reading of fixing a claim. Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: In row_rules.water_rules, a channel-map farm passes when its channel ends in its frame or a private well stands in its frame; the claim cites 0031's rule, with a parenthetical for the well-map case.
decisions.why: This widens what the check accepts so it matches 0031's text ('a farm the channel cannot be led to is given a well'). It does not carve anything out of the GM's request: no amendment asks the check to keep refusing a well-watered farm, and the research it conforms to is cited. The well-map parenthetical describes the existing branch and adds no behavior. Not a fidelity finding, but worth noting: the check as written accepts a well even where a channel could have reached the farm, while the claim says 'where no channel reaches it'. Whether that check-to-claim gap is IN-STEP is for the claims check to judge.

decisions.summary: street_arrives asks, on a row's street or off it, whether the way's point nearest the HOUSE serves the farm under end_serves (60 ft of the house or 12 ft of its built ground); lay_door_paths and row_rules' farm_not_on_its_street read that one predicate

decisions.summary: the new part B after the arbiter's 'continue' ruling: no new route or change, next step the claims check, gate and landing
decisions.why: Decides nothing new; records that the change is D125's and follows the ruling's named step.

decisions.summary: A claims finding carried by T96's claims round (access.py::ACCESS_HALF_FT#corridor room, DRIFTED) becomes its own task instead of widening T96.
decisions.why: The request's claims work (Amendment 7, ten more claims) and FR-013/FR-015 (a carried finding is carried, not refused; a second goal found in a task becomes its own task) cover it; Amendment 6 asks that obvious improvements be made along the way. It adds no behavior.

Bringing the comment into step and leaving the code alone narrows nothing that was asked.
