decisions.summary: One goal: the comment is corrected and the claim's re-check returns IN-STEP.
decisions.why: One goal per task (FR-015). The success test is the claims check that found the drift, not a new verification.

decisions.summary: A discrepancy found while working T101 (the two 7 ft figures on 0246's drawing page measure differently) is split off as its own task rather than folded into T101.
decisions.why: FR-015 (a second goal found in a task becomes its own task) and amendment 3's option 3 (a finding becomes an open task the feature cannot close without) carry it; the GM's request asks each task to keep one goal and be measured on its own.

decisions.summary: A new block on 0246's drawing page saying the room's 7 ft is counted to the tread's edge and the least gap's 7 ft to the lane's middle; both existing blocks kept as written, nothing renumbered.
decisions.why: The GM's request never speaks to these figures, and the block preserves no behavior he asked to change. Item 3 marks both figures as ours (O) and the block says so ('map drawing conventions'). Its arithmetic matches item 4's measured reading: 7 + 4 + 7 = 18, the middle at 7 + 2 = 9 ft, 2 ft above the least gap of 7.

decisions.summary: Code is left alone: MIN_WEB_GAP = 2 x WEB_FABRIC_GAP + 4 already encodes the room's convention and WEB_FABRIC_GAP the gap's.
decisions.why: The code already agrees with the block D127 adds, so a page-only change is the whole of the goal; nothing the GM asked for goes undone.

decisions.summary: The block is written first, then the record checks and claims triage it owes (T31's lesson).
decisions.why: Sequencing inside the task; it adds the checks the project already owes a new block and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: T109 exists as its own task for a finding made while working T107 (the grove fallback's band gap and two GUESS touch claims)
decisions.why: FR-015 (a second goal becomes its own task) and amendment 3's option 3 (a finding becomes an open task the feature cannot close without); the change is unchanged since its last CLEAR verdict.

decisions.summary: In _thread_the_fabric the grove bands the fallback routes round and clips against are grown by CONNECTOR_BAND_GAP_FT - FOOTPATH_FABRIC_GAP (5.5 ft) a side, so the line keeps 12.5 ft off the trees; crops keep their own gap; the claim cites 0036
decisions.why: Unchanged since its CLEAR verdict: it conforms the code to 0036's working room, counted once as T98's D119 did, with no constant's value moved.

decisions.summary: The same band growth applies wherever the function tests the fabric - its first route, its clip and its checks - so no route keeps a band at 7 ft
decisions.why: Widens the fix to the rest of the function, and only toward the task's stated goal (Approach item 1, the track and spur keep 0036's room off a grove). It narrows nothing the GM asked for and carves out no case. It follows a measured DRIFTED finding on the first route (labeled measured 2026-10-19, the claims round, cohort 16 of 16).

decisions.summary: The two touch claims (touch._one_network, touch._touch_junctions) say the routed link keeps WEB_FABRIC_GAP (7 ft to the middle), labeled DEVIATION on 0246 as _route's own claim already is; the junction link's 25 ft is cited to 0081's join reach
decisions.why: The earlier CLEAR text already decided that these claims describe the gap the code routes at instead of changing the code. The DEVIATION label states that existing departure honestly, the same way _route's own claim does, and it neither moves behavior nor exempts anything new. The 0081 citation replaces a GUESS with a source.

decisions.summary: Part B owed by the arbiter's continue ruling: nothing refusing, no new decision beyond D128, the ruling's two asides filed as T110 and T111
decisions.why: It records the ruling's next step and adds no decision. Filing the asides as their own tasks is FR-015's rule, and those tasks are not decided here.

decisions.summary: One goal: a reader of 0246's drawing page meeting 'Enoshima' can learn what it is where they meet it; done when the glossary holds Enoshima, the built record shows its tooltip on 0246, record-format finds the word ruled, and no block is edited.
decisions.why: A second goal found while working T107 (an FR-020 ranking row, amendment 7's 'ten more claims') split into its own task, as FR-015 (amendment 4's 'one goal per task', approved verbatim) requires. It finishes a finding of the requested work and adds no scope beyond it.

decisions.summary: A glossary tooltip, leaving 0246's block untouched; a gloss written inside the block was weighed and refused because the block's claims would then owe full checks.
decisions.why: This picks how to meet the goal and narrows nothing the GM asked for. research/CLAUDE.md, quoted as the constraint, already makes a glossary tooltip the place for a term the reader would not know. The request says nothing about rewording 0246's block, so leaving it alone excludes nothing he asked for. The reason given, avoiding re-checks the change would not need, serves the request's stated aim of cutting the time a task takes.

decisions.summary: Glossary file l7r/diagram/interactive/assets/glossary/9995-enoshima.json, worded from Morse's 1886 description quoted in 0081's notes.
decisions.why: This carries out exit (c): one file per term in the one shared glossary, as the quoted constraint requires. Whether the wording is accurate (for example 'small island town', which is not in the quoted Morse passage) is a matter for the record checks this task's order runs, not a fidelity finding.

decisions.summary: Glossary file, then make glossary, then the record checks it owes; budget 20 minutes.
decisions.why: This sequences and budgets the one goal and decides nothing the request or spec left open in a way that narrows them. Items 10 and 11 are n/a and decide nothing.

decisions.summary: In tick-task.landed_refusal, a task with no land-tooling run is refused when a commit ahead of origin/main touches a file outside specs/ and dev/.
decisions.why: It changes D98's last sentence (a task with no row is not refused) in the widening direction only: more enforcement, nothing the GM asked or the accepted spec settled is narrowed. It serves the GM's 'implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way' (amendment 6) and 'make our tooling do the thing correctly automatically every time' (amendment 8), and FR-010's guard-not-reminder rule.

decisions.summary: Files under specs/ and dev/ (the feature's own records, the landing's run logs) are not counted by the new refusal.
decisions.why: A carve-out from a refusal that did not exist before: D98 refused nothing for a task with no row, so excluding these directories narrows nothing the GM asked or the spec settled. It is what lets the guard run at all mid-feature, where every clone carries unlanded specs/ commits (the tick itself writes one).

decisions.summary: The work's presence on main decides the tick, not the landing route's own log; the log was weighed and refused.
decisions.why: A design choice about how the new check reads the world; it narrows no request or requirement, and the block records the alternative and why it was refused.

decisions.summary: The refusal names the file and the one command that lands it (scripts/sync-with-main.sh done).
decisions.why: The same shape FR-019 and SC-009 set for this feature's refusals (each names its one command).

decisions.summary: A tests/tooling/ test red without the change.
decisions.why: Pure enforcement of D130: with D130 deleted the test has nothing left to check.

decisions.summary: connector_dry_exit runs its fill twice (water lines as walls; and open within FORD_HALF of each brook_fords crossing place) and takes the crossing way only where the own-bank fill finds none or the own-bank way is longer by more than BROOK_CROSSING_COST_FT (0035's 150 ft); the claim cites 0035's crossing places and its keep-to-own-bank rule; no page edit.
decisions.why: A claim fix of the kind the GM pulled into this feature (Amendments 6-7, FR-020). The change since the last CLEAR verdict tightens the crossing to 0035's own stated rule (a way keeps to its own bank unless crossing saves about 150 ft), the same constant the track's own router already uses; it carves nothing out of the request, and the fill's ability to cross only at a crossing place is unchanged. The guess status of the 150 ft is recorded on 0035's page and the claim cites it, satisfying the request's guardrail that a rule's reason be recorded where the code changes.

decisions.summary: Exit (c), a new rule - the fill passes the brook at crossing places - chosen; (b) principled exception and (e) conform-as-claimed refused.
decisions.why: Unchanged from the CLEAR text; the checklist's three named exits are judged as the approved proposal asks, and the chosen exit brings the code toward the research page rather than away from it.

decisions.summary: A task's time is its tick window: from the tick before to its own tick, booked to the task(s) ticked at its end; the table gains the window's wall-clock minutes.
decisions.why: Amendment 10: the GM asked for tooling to gather 'this kind of information' - the per-task timing he had just been answered with, which was tick-to-tick spans. Reporting that span by one command is the request.

decisions.summary: Tick times are read by the tool from tasks.md's git history (the commit that turned a box [x]) rather than from the event log's tick records.
decisions.why: This departs from the measurement as recorded in request.md ('read from the event log (each tick now records its task, hour 33's fix) as a report, not rebuilt from git history by hand'): the plan rebuilds from git history, by tool, and does not use the event log's tick records. Within because the GM's own words name no source, the recorded objection is to the HAND rebuild and this is one command, and both sources deliver the information asked for - which one is design. Noted: the plan's step 4 measured the lagging active mark, not the hour-33 tick records, so the named source was set aside unmeasured (git history does reach ticks from before that fix).

decisions.summary: Tasks ticked in one commit share one window, reported as e.g. 'T96+T98'.
decisions.why: The measure the GM was answered with already reported T96 with T98 jointly (1 h 34). The joint window follows from D132-source's choice of git history, not from a physical limit - per-task tick records could separate a batch - but it reports every task, truthfully, and drops none.

decisions.summary: Gaps inside each window are bucketed by where_time.tables (T89/T90's buckets) as now, with no name-based booking.
decisions.why: 'Where did its time go' is the other half of the information the GM was given (claims rounds, landing cost, plan reviews); existing buckets are reused, and dropping name-based booking removes only the lagging attribution step 4 measured wrong.

decisions.summary: A new BY=tick mode of where-time rather than mending the active mark.
decisions.why: The request asks for the information gathered by tooling, not for the mark to be repaired; the mechanism inside that is design, not scope.

decisions.summary: Per-task time is printed by make where-time BY=tick, not by make feature-report's per-task table (FR-005, SC-001), which the blocks do not name.
decisions.why: The GM's words ask for 'tooling adjustments' and name no command; a where-time mode adds a report beside FR-005's table and removes nothing FR-005 or SC-001 require. Not a narrowing of the accepted spec, though the plan would read better naming FR-005.

decisions.summary: Done: make where-time F=385 BY=tick [SINCE=] prints each task's span and bucket minutes, T97 within a minute of the hand count's 53, with a tests/tooling test red without it.
decisions.why: A check that the requested report gives the right number and keeps doing so enforces the request (GM 2026-09-20); nothing beyond the report is verified.

decisions.summary: Every 'code changed' claim not already named touched is owed only a code triage (diff hunks of the unit vs origin/main plus its claims); named claims go to impl-drift, the rest cleared at new code/core fingerprints; no claim-count threshold.
decisions.why: Amendment 10's first lever verbatim: 're-check only the claim lines a change touched'. The triage is how 'touched' is decided, copying 318 FR-016's page triage; round 1's unmeasured CODE_TRIAGE_MIN carve-out is gone ('whatever the number of claims its unit carries'). Refusing a static name match re-checks more than a literal reading would, which is conservative and serves the lever's purpose rather than narrowing it. A new claim going to impl-drift is not a re-check at all.

decisions.summary: A unit whose fingerprint moved but has no diff hunk against origin/main to show is owed in full (forced).
decisions.why: Without a hunk there is nothing to read to tell which claims a change touched, so the lever cannot be applied to that unit. Owing in full is the existing behavior for the case where the rule cannot run, not a carve-out from a case where it could.

decisions.summary: owed, research_why, relabeled_only and helpers move from claims.py to claims_owed.py, re-exported, to hold the 1,000-line bar.
decisions.why: A structural move to keep the GM's standing 1,000-line bar (2026-08-31). It changes nothing in what was asked.

decisions.summary: tick-task.py's refusals become one function refusal(root, d, task, note, landed=True); a new make land-batch F= T="T1 T2" NOTE= asks it of every task (landed=False) and refuses before anything lands, runs scripts/sync-with-main.sh done once, and on exit 0 ticks each task with 'landed in batch T1+T2: <NOTE>' (the landed refusal then asked of each); a failed landing ticks none.
decisions.why: Amendment 10 approves 'batch the gate and the landing cohort across two or three small engine fixes'. One run of the gated route (make done, make cohort-landing, the claims gate) for several tasks is exactly that; every per-task tick refusal is kept, asked before landing and the landed refusal (D130) asked after, so nothing the request did not ask to relax is relaxed. The batch size is left to the caller rather than capped, which narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: landed_refusal's message for engine work off main adds 'or, with the next small fix, make land-batch'.
decisions.why: Points the existing refusal at the requested batching route; it changes no refusal's reach, only names the command that serves the request.

decisions.summary: A command that lands and ticks a batch, not a CLAUDE.md practice.
decisions.why: Implements the requested lever as tooling; the alternative refused is weaker than the request, not part of it.

decisions.id: Approach-2 (the gated route stays the only way engine code lands)
decisions.summary: Batching goes through scripts/sync-with-main.sh done, never around it.
decisions.why: The GM asked to batch the gate and the cohort, not to skip either; keeping the route is the request's own premise.

decisions.summary: Approach items 1/9: a task that only rewords (a claim relabeled, a comment, a glossary entry) goes from Approach to tick without a spec-fidelity plan review; a task that decides anything still gets one.
decisions.why: Amendment 10's third suggestion, approved by the GM ('implement all 3 of your suggestions'), verbatim: 'skip the plan review for wording-only tasks that decide nothing new'. The suggestion was offered against the wording-only claim-fix tasks timed at 5-15 min, which is the class item 4 names (T31, T103, T105, T110). Keeping the review for any task that decides keeps the 'decide nothing new' half of the clause.

decisions.summary: A Decisions block of one '**Wording only.** <what>' line makes plan_gate.block_status skip the section, and make decide says no review is owed and builds no bundle; any '**D<n> - ' line in the same block undoes the declaration.
decisions.why: This is the skip itself, mechanized in the existing plan gate the way D94's quiet part B already is. The undo rule narrows the exemption to sections that decide nothing, which is the request's own condition, not a carve-out from it.

decisions.summary: make tick refuses a wording-only task when a non-merge commit since its last make task-start changed a file outside specs/ and dev/ that is neither a glossary JSON entry nor a .py file with unchanged semantic_bytes; a research page's block counts as a decision and is refused the same way.
decisions.why: Its only effect is to make 'wording-only ... decide nothing new' true of every task that skips the review: it refuses work that changed what runs under a wording declaration. That is enforcement of the requested condition (the GM 2026-09-20 rule on checks that make the asked-for thing happen), and the GM's standing rule 'a tool, never a reminder' that the Approach cites. It reaches no other agent, command or default beyond the tick of a task that declared itself wording-only. Its allowlist (specs/, dev/, glossary JSON, .py with unchanged semantic_bytes) is the mechanical boundary of 'wording only': anything outside it, including prose files elsewhere, stays reviewed. That errs toward keeping review, matching the claim-fix class (claims, comments, glossary) the suggestion was offered against, so it is not a narrowing of the skip the GM approved.

decisions.summary: Approach item 6: a declaration checked by the tick against the diff, chosen over an agent classifying the section.
decisions.why: An agent classification would be the very review the GM asked to skip for these tasks; choosing the mechanical check is a means, not a change of what was asked.

decisions.summary: Approach items 5/9: tests in tests/tooling/ red without the exemption and the tick check.
decisions.why: Verification of the requested behavior only; nothing beyond the request is measured or proven.

decisions.summary: A ruling carrying tooling_fix is refused without fix_measure (compiling regex over main-session Bash commands, or agent:<kind>) and fix_minutes; the 45 fixes made before T119 get a measure assigned from their own sentence in specs/<feature>/fix-measures.json (no fix_minutes, as their cost was never measured); the one declined fix is reported declined; a fix meant to save editing/reading/model time is measured through the command or check it shortens.
decisions.why: Change 3 asks that each fix's yield be measured against the time it was meant to save. Round 1's narrowing (46 earlier fixes reported 'unmeasured', i.e. excluded) is gone: every fix that was made now has a measure and enters the yield report (item 9 confirms 'the 45 made before T119 included'). Reading a sentence to choose WHAT to measure is not the refused exit of item 6 (judging the yield from the text); the yield itself is still computed from the transcripts. The declined fix was never made, so there is no yield to measure - not a carve-out from 'each fix'. Leaving fix_minutes empty on the old rows removes nothing from the yield, which D140 computes from before/after rates, not from fix_minutes. The proxy sentence is a measurement method that still measures every fix, not an exclusion.

decisions.summary: scripts/measure/fix_yield.py (make fix-yield F=<n>): per fix settled done, the measure's rate per session hour over YIELD_BEFORE_HOURS before its ruling and since its settling; 'saves nothing' / 'too early' / 'saving'.
decisions.why: This is change 3 itself - each fix's yield against the time it was meant to save, measured by a tool rather than estimated.

decisions.summary: The step-back bundle carries the table as fix-yield.md; the arbiter's contract asks of it: a fix that saves nothing is retired as that hour's tooling_fix, or kept with the reason recorded.
decisions.why: Puts the measurement where the hourly step-back reads it (cadence unchanged, as the GM required); retiring a fix that saves nothing is change 2's 'removing or simplifying comes before adding' applied to the yield. It narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: YIELD_MIN_HOURS = 3 and YIELD_BEFORE_HOURS = 6 as new tooling windows.
decisions.why: Window choices for a measurement the GM asked for; they exclude no fix and do not touch the hourly cadence.

decisions.summary: plan_bundle.build passes each earlier text with the verdict the record holds for it (tasks.<id>.verdict or blocks.<key>.verdict), marks it <!-- block "<key>" verdict X --> (CLEAR, BLOCKED or 'no verdict recorded'), heads earlier.md 'Each changed block's text when last judged, with that verdict', and the MANIFEST sentence says the same; the alternative of showing only CLEAR texts is refused.
decisions.why: A tooling correctness fix: the bundle's heading claims every earlier text was ruled CLEAR while it can show a BLOCKED one (the premise is visible in this very bundle's earlier.md heading, 'at its last CLEAR verdict'). Labeling the truth removes nothing a reviewer was given and narrows no clause of the request; it serves amendment 6's 'implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way' and amendment 8's 'make our tooling do the thing correctly automatically every time'. Refusing the CLEAR-only option keeps the round-1 BLOCKED text in front of the round-2 reviewer, which preserves rather than narrows what plan review reads.

decisions.summary: a test under tests/tooling/ red without the verdict heading and per-block verdict line
decisions.why: Enforcement of D142 only: delete D142 and the test has nothing to check (GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: A guard-file bypass found working T117 (a python heredoc wrote the Makefile through open(p, "w") with no refusal) is fixed as its own task.
decisions.why: The GM asked that obvious tooling improvements be made along the way (amendment 6) and that a tooling fix carry a measured cost or a defect that reached main (amendment 10, change 1); this is a measured defect (2026-10-19, T117's heredoc wrote a guard file unrefused) in a guard on main. It is split from T117 per the one-goal rule the GM approved (amendment 4). It adds no GM-facing behavior: it makes an existing rule (guard files edited only through make guard-edit) hold for a write route it missed.

decisions.summary: hm_make's raw python-write patterns gain open("<guard>", "w"|"a"|"x").
decisions.why: Closes a measured gap in an existing guard rule; refuses only what the rule already forbids. Amendment 10 change 2 (simplify a misfiring guard before adding one) is not engaged: no new guard is added, and the existing one under-fires rather than misfires.

decisions.summary: _GUARD_BIND also binds a name to a plain string literal naming a guard path; that name then counts as a write through open(<name>, "w"|"a"|"x") or .write_text(.
decisions.why: This is exactly the T117 shape (p="Makefile"; open(p,"w").write(...)); same rule, same reach.

decisions.id: Exit (c) / reads and mentions stay legal
decisions.summary: The match is widened by the measured shapes only; refusing any python heredoc that names a guard file was weighed and refused; open(p) and open(p, "r") stay legal.
decisions.why: Keeps feature 164's standing rule (a guard filename's presence is never a write). Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed: the request asks for no guard reach here, and this choice keeps the guard from refusing work it does not concern.

decisions.summary: In land-tooling.sh's D46 conflict branch, before git merge --abort, the conflicted files whose last origin/main commit is this clone's own 'Tooling from <clone>,' landing are named in the refusal with the line that keeps the clone's side (sync-in, then git checkout --ours, git add, git commit --no-edit, land again); the merge is still aborted and the landing still refused; the tool resolves nothing.
decisions.why: D46's behavior (a conflicting merge aborted, the clone left as it was, the refusal naming sync-in to resolve by hand) is unchanged; D144 only adds information to that refusal. It is an obvious tooling improvement found while working (amendment 6: 'implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way') and it is exactly the binding change-route of the round arbiter on hour:385-approach-checklist@35 ('T122 narrows to a message'). Amendment 10 change 1's 10-minute measured-cost bar governs step-back tooling fixes; T122 was found working T119, and the arbiter, which named the hazard sub-bar, bound this narrower route anyway - that is the arbiter's call, reviewed by the GM after landing (feature 379), not a decision of this plan.

decisions.summary: The earlier resolver (scripts/gates/self_landed.py taking the clone's side and committing the merge) is withdrawn; T122 only names and instructs.
decisions.why: The GM never asked for a resolver, so withdrawing it narrows nothing he asked for; it returns T122 to D46 as written (a conflicting merge is aborted and refused, resolved by hand), which the earlier BLOCKED version had departed from.

decisions.summary: A conflicted file counts as self-landed when git log -1 --format=%s origin/main -- <file> begins 'Tooling from <this clone's name>,'.
decisions.why: A design detail of D144 that implements the arbiter's words 'each conflicting file whose main-side commit is this clone's own land-tooling commit' literally; it changes no behavior beyond the refusal's text.

decisions.id: Done (item 9): other conflicts refused as now; test red without it
decisions.summary: Any other conflict is refused exactly as today; tests/hooks/test-land-tooling.sh gains a case red without D144.
decisions.why: The first keeps D46 unchanged; the second is a test that only fails when the requested refusal text is absent - enforcement of what was asked, not new scope.

decisions.summary: plan_bundle._QUALIFIED accepts an optional 'amendment <n>' (with its own optional comma) and an optional opening parenthesis between the feature number and the id, so 'Feature 375 amendment 11 (D64)' and '375 amendment 6, FR-002' resolve from feature 375.
decisions.why: Repairs a measured defect in D85/D91 (a qualified citation of another feature's decision read as this feature's same-numbered one, handing the reviewer the wrong text); it serves D85's own stated purpose that the reviewer reads what the block names. Tooling fix of the kind amendment 6 ('implement any obvious performance / tooling / process improvements along the way') asks for; it narrows nothing - an unqualified id stays the reviewed feature's, and the test only enforces the fix.

decisions.summary: Exit chosen: widen the qualified form by the measured shape, rather than requiring blocks to rewrite citations into the existing forms.
decisions.why: A choice of mechanism for the fix; it removes no case the request or D85/D91 cover and adds no behavior beyond reading the citation the block wrote.

decisions.summary: 0246's back-lane bullet reworded: a back lane is laid about 30 ft past the last house it serves (the room it is cut in) and its end then pulled back to that house like every end reaching nothing; the frame claim cites that with the page path written out in full
decisions.why: Conforms the record to what the code draws, an exit the request names (line 43, 'at least three exits besides conform', and the GM's point that arbitrary numbers should be inspected rather than obeyed). The 30 ft is the page's own GUESS, and its general rule already says ends are pulled back; no behavior, constant or requested scope is narrowed. The round-2 change only writes out the abbreviated page path; the decision is unchanged.

decisions.summary: a new rule to overrun the trim by 30 ft is weighed and refused
decisions.why: Keeps the current drawn behavior (the 2026-09-27 trim), exactly the kind of exit weighing the checklist asks for; it carves no case out of anything the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: to_its_joints returns list(street) where fewer than two joints stand on it (len(at) < 2); its docstring reads 'fewer than two joints'
decisions.why: It carries out the task's own filed goal (a one-joint street left whole, not cut to a point) under the claim-fix work the GM approved (amendments 6 and 7, FR-020). The request says nothing about street geometry, so nothing it asks for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Cutting a one-joint street to its joint and the farther door was weighed and refused, because trim_streets already passes the door anchors among the ends
decisions.why: A design choice between two ways of reaching the same goal. Nothing the GM asked for is given up, and choosing between them is not a fidelity question.

decisions.summary: T132 lands with T125 by make land-batch
decisions.why: This is the second lever of amendment 10 ('batch the gate and the landing cohort across two or three small engine fixes'), which the GM approved.

decisions.summary: stage_web's house list becomes list(s.M.get("houses", [])): the dead `role != "headman" or True` test is deleted, so the code says what it already does (every house served), behavior unchanged; excluding the headman's house was weighed and refused.
decisions.why: The task is an impl-drift finding the gate filed as an open task under the GM's Amendment 3 ruling ("lock in option three": findings filed as open tasks, fixed before the feature closes). Making the code state its existing behavior fixes the drift without changing any map; the refused alternative (dropping the headman's house) would have been the behavior change, and the plan cites 0246's page for every farmhouse being served. Nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: _web_cut_lines gains a GUESS claim for the cross-lane tie's 30 ft run past the outermost back lane, citing 0246's drawing page and saying the page gives no distance.
decisions.why: Labeling an unclaimed rendering figure is what the claims round owed under the GM's Amendment 3 ruling (the gate files each finding as an open task, fixed before the feature closes) and the approved checklist's 'Where does it come from? ... If it's ours, it's a knob'. It labels the 30 ft honestly as ours (a GUESS, the page silent on the distance) rather than dressing it as research. No value moves and no requested behavior is excepted.
